Billionaires donated millions of dollars to a political action committee, Building a Better California, working to defeat the measure. The committee, which backed other measures on the ballot designed to nullify the tax, raised more than $333 million, nearly a third of which came from Brin.

Brin, along with his fellow Google co-founder Larry Page, was among the billionaires who started cutting ties with the state in anticipation of the possible tax. Another tech mogul, Mark Zuckerberg, said he would remain in the state for eight years and made a deal with Meta to help him pay the tax without losing his ownership stake in the company.

Some traditional Democratic allies, including Planned Parenthood and the California Medical Association, were part of a coalition opposing it. They were concerned about how the tax revenue would be divvied up and about the potential impact on the state’s budget if there was a mass exodus of wealthy taxpayers. California’s budget relies heavily on the income tax of the state’s richest residents.

“Proposition 40 was a reckless experiment conducted on our state’s economy with little regard for the harms it would cause,” the coalition said in a statement.

Robert Swonger, an auto glass technician living near Sacramento who’s politically independent, said before voting concluded Nov. 3 that he planned to vote against it.

“Obviously, I would like billionaires not to have as much money as they do,” he said. “But I don’t believe taxing them out of existence is going to work.”

Progressive politicians, including Sanders and Massachusetts Sen. Elizabeth Warren, have long supported a federal wealth tax. Newsom says a California wealth tax would disadvantage the state, but he supports a national minimum tax on anyone with a net worth above $100 million.

Days before Sanders held rallies in California cities last month, Newsom told reporters that the senator’s focus on wealth inequality was “spot-on.” But he said that “on this issue, we fundamentally disagree.”

Supporters of the California tax started running ads recently in New Hampshire, New Mexico and Virginia, states that will vote early in the Democratic presidential primary in 2028, that criticize Newsom for his opposition to the measure.

News.title: Faced with influx, prosecutor in Washington says he lacks resources to defend immigration cases
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Faced with an influx of petitions by people alleging they're being unlawfully detained by federal immigration authorities, the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Western District of Washington said Monday that it no longer has the manpower to defend every case and will let judges rule without government opposition.

Acting U.S. Attorney Charles Floyd said in a letter to U.S. District Judge David Estudillo that habeas corpus cases initiate “protracted litigation” with numerous hearings, briefings and motions that consume prosecutors' resources.

“Thus, going forward, in order to conserve resources, there will be many habeas cases in which the USAO will no longer assume responsibility for providing a defense on behalf of the respondents," Floyd wrote.

The backlog has “severely impacted the government's ability to respond” to immigration petitions and prevented prosecutors from dealing with other unrelated civil litigation, he said. As a result, his office will decline to defend “many” habeas cases. He didn't specify how many cases could be affected.

Judges have often ruled against the administration in cases filed by tens of thousands of detainees arguing that they were being held illegally by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. It has been a source of great frustration to administration officials — and to judges and advocates who say ICE has trampled on individual rights amid the Trump administration’s hardline immigration agenda.

Last week, U.S. border czar Tom Homan told Fox News that courts have been weighed down by about 85,000 immigration habeas cases as the government carries out a sweeping crackdown.

Floyd is a former judge who, along with three other Washington judges, advocated for prohibiting immigration courts from granting bond to detainees — a question that is now before the U.S. Supreme Court.

The justices will consider whether immigrants who have been living in the U.S. have a right to a hearing to determine if they should remain detained while challenging their possible deportation.

Most appeals courts to have considered the issue have found that it violates federal law to detain immigrants, including those living in the U.S. illegally, without a bond hearing. Those decisions conflict with rulings by the 5th and 8th circuits, which held that immigrants accused of illegally entering and remaining in the U.S. must be detained while their deportation cases are pending.

News.title: Fears over Ebola spread in DRC as patients flee attack on treatment centre
News.content:
A statement from the health body said: “Health facilities have been attacked and patients, including hundreds people with confirmed or suspected Ebola infection, have fled in search of safety raise serious public health concerns.



“In an Ebola outbreak, every interruption to patient care, contact tracing and disease surveillance creates additional risks for communities already facing extraordinary hardship.



“People must be able to seek treatment safely, and health workers must be able to deliver essential services without fear of violence.”



The body called for a “corridor of peace, protection of civilians, patients, health workers and health facilities, and for safe, sustained access to affected communities”.



The ADF is one of the most feared of scores of armed militia operating in eastern DRC.



The group was originally formed in Uganda in the 1990s by people accusing the government of persecuting Muslims. The army routed the group and the remnants fled across the border, starting a campaign of terror in DRC, before swearing allegiance to IS in late 2018.



The group has since become notorious for its bloody attacks on civilians, which human rights groups say have amounted to war crimes or crimes against humanity.



Earlier this year, Amnesty International, said that advances by the separate Rwanda-backed March 23 movement (M23) militant group in the same region had left Congolese forces overstretched. The ADF had been able to increase attacks in the resulting security vacuum.



The charity said the great majority of victims were Congolese Christians, but the ADF also kills local Muslims who disagree with their interpretation of Islam.



Officials said the attackers struck the village about 30 miles west of Beni around 11 pm local time ‌on Thursday, officials said.



The medical director of the Kelele hospital, Dr Christian Kakule Vulembera, told Radio Okapi, a UN-backed radio station: “Around midnight, the hospital emptied of its patients. All the patients left, including those who were in isolation for suspected Ebola virus infection.”

Attempts to curb the Ebola outbreak have been undermined by suspicion and poor security, with local people frequently turning on health workers.



Conspiracy theories are rife that the outbreak is a hoax to enrich aid agencies, or alternatively that health workers are spreading the disease for their own ends.



Doctors Without Borders, the medical aid charity, over the weekend condemned an attempted arson attack targeting an Ebola treatment centre in Biautu, Beni, North Kivu, where 36 patients were hospitalised.

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: Man Utd are in relegation trouble and Carrick must be sacked
News.content:
Michael Carrick says he has been given no assurances about his future beyond this afternoon’s crucial game against Aston Villa at Old Trafford.



United are searching for only their second Premier League win of the season and first in 70 days after the club’s worst start to a campaign for 40 years piled the pressure on Carrick.



They dropped into the relegation zone last night following Nottingham Forest’s victory over Manchester City and will be bottom by the end of the weekend if they lose to Villa and Crystal Palace and Sunderland both win.



The Old Trafford hierarchy opted to give Carrick more time to try to turn their season around following a 3-0 hammering by Bournemouth and 4-1 drubbing in Como, since when United have been beaten 2-0 by Chelsea and recovered from two goals down to overcome Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday night.



Asked if he had been told outright he would still be in charge next week, Carrick said: “No - no. Just carry on as absolute normal.”



Pressed on when he felt his future was uncertain, the head coach added: “No, no. Whatever happens and what’s going to happen is going to happen in terms of the game, we’ve got to prepare right.



“I’m really looking forward to playing at home on the back of the other night. The supporters are hopefully looking forward to coming and energised and feeling good about what they might see and we’ve got to repay that.”



Another defeat would leave the United board with a big decision to make around Carrick’s future at a time when they are under severe attack from the fanbase.



United’s game against Roma was briefly interrupted when tennis balls were thrown on to the pitch in the first half of a game notable for more furious protests against the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe.



Three people were arrested by Greater Manchester Police for throwing items on to the pitch and are understood to have been hit with automatic three-year football banning orders as a consequence.



More in-stadium demonstrations are expected today with regular match going fans encouraged not to buy alcohol or drinks inside Old Trafford and again release green and gold balloons before kick-off.



Green and gold were the club’s original colours as Newton Heath and have become a symbol of protest against the ownership.



Asked why there had been such a big drop-off from last season, Carrick added: “It’s just inconsistency, that’s within games,” he said.



“It can be a number of things, it’s never just one thing: a bit of decision-making, a bit of concentration, things going against us in certain points, sometimes we haven’t helped ourselves. So there’s no excuses for it, it is what it is. The great thing is we can do something about it.”

News.title: Energised England deliver statement win to take heat off Borthwick
News.content:
England’s players delivered on their self-created ultimatum to “do it for Steve” by annihilating an abysmal Australia. Barring an extraordinary sequence of events, Borthwick will now remain as head coach through to the World Cup.

Even if Rugby Football Union chief executive Bill Sweeney’s vote of confidence in the head coach last week was delivered without caveats, he would still have been forced to play the role of reluctant Caesar if the crowd turned mutinous, as they did four years ago. That resulted in Sweeney delivering the thumbs down on Eddie Jones’s reign.

Yet this did not come to pass, as England showed plenty of fire and fury on behalf of their head coach after his control of the dressing room was questioned last week. With 14 minutes to go the crowd, who had been muted on Remembrance Sunday, broke into a rendition of Swing Low, indicating their own approval.

It was not perfect. Attack coach Lee Blackett will be hugely frustrated that they only scored seven tries from a staggering 22 entries into the Australia 22. They also took their foot off the Wallabies’ throats in the final quarter, although they did surpass their highest points total against the visitors. Probably the biggest disappointment was the injuries suffered by wing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and centre Seb Atkinson, who had both enjoyed strong games until that point.

News.title: Lando Norris wins chaotic Sao Paulo Grand Prix but F1 season is fizzling out
News.content:
Lando Norris will start today’s Sao Paulo Grand Prix on pole position after a chaotic qualifying session at Interlagos yesterday. A red flag was thrown a matter of moments into qualifying, which led to a lengthy delay of around an hour and a half. When racing did resume, the conditions were treacherous but it was the 2025 world champion Norris who coped best by claiming his third straight pole at Interlagos.

“It has been a long day,” Norris said after taking pole. “It has been a great qualifying. To be on pole again here, two years in a row, different conditions to last year, but I am very happy. It is not easy conditions out there, especially when you know it is going to rain a lot more. It was about getting two laps in at the beginning, not making any mistakes, and that is exactly what we did, so it has been a very good day.

“This was my first time driving the car in the wet, so I think I figured it out pretty quick. It is tough because you are wet, intermediates, all different tyres, and it was very windy the last couple of laps. It was certainly a good day for learning for me and good to take into tomorrow [today]. These guys [Mercedes] are also very quick. Just happy. Today [yesterday] is about getting on pole. It does not really matter how you do it, so very pleased with that.”

News.title: Chelsea bullied by Brian Brobbey and Sunderland
News.content:
Today is must-win match: for both sides.

For Sunderland that argument is easy to make – they are bottom of the Premier League, are without a win since August and for morale, if nothing else need at least a point, though three is really what the doctor orders.

For Chelsea – fourth in the table and with three wins in their past four league outings – the argument that this is a must-win game is harder to make, but bear with me here...

Facing a Sunderland team who are suffering from the worst of both worlds – blunt in attack and pitiful in defence (what a difference from last season...) and have proven all too easy to beat (as their 2-0 home defeat Zagreb illustrated on Thursday) – the west Londoners are expected to win. Fail to return to the capital with the three points and there will once again be question marks over Xabi Alonso’s side. They are flaky and flashy in equal measure, able to play and win well in spurts, but once again unable to mount sustained pressure needed for a title challenge and forced to battle it out for the hope of a top-four spot at best. Those will be the arguments raised should they not win this afternoon.

The hosts doubtless wish that their ‘issues’ were as golden as today’s opposition. For Trai Hume, who scored in this fixture last season, the Sunderland players are at fault for the sorry start to the season and he wants to put right the wrongs so far, starting today.

“I couldn’t tell you what’s changed. We thought we’d addressed it after the Leeds game, where we were aggressive, strong, but we go out there tonight and see the old habits of the start of the season. Everything’s a bit laboured, and it’s something the staff can’t fix, it’s on us as players,” Hume said.

“We’re still together as a club, as a team. I think the run of form we’re on, it would be easy to think we’re not, but we are. We are really upset with how we’ve been playing, and the results don’t lie. We haven’t been good enough and we know that. We have to address that.”

Stay here for all the team news, build-up and action.

News.title: Liverpool’s expensive attack feast on Palace to leave Sage looking doomed
News.content:
Major signings need to lay down a marker when arriving at Liverpool. Barcola has his hat-trick at LASK in the Champions League, but we are still waiting for a stirring big-match-defining contribution from him since his summer arrival. Arguably the same could be said for Wirtz, nearly 18 months since he joined.

Neither left Selhurst Park looking like the world-beaters they did occasionally for their previous clubs. Still, one misfiring attacker creating a goal for another represents progress and all great partnerships must start somewhere. Lennon and McCartney would improve after 1958’s Too Bad About Sorrows.

If there was ever a place for the least-productive expensively assembled attacking group in the league to find form it was surely south London on this Sunday lunchtime. Liverpool came in with two defeats in their previous two but, European trophy aside, it has been a lousy 2026 for Palace.

They have the most defeats of any ever-present Premier League team and began (and ended) the weekend with the worst defensive record. They have conceded twice as many goals from headers as any other team. Even their most loyal fan group has disbanded.

Alexis Mac Allister opened the scoring in gut-punching fashion, after a series of Palace near-misses. Chairman Steve Parish rubbed his face in the directors’ box, in the style of peak-stress era Guardiola. None of this looked good for Sage, who appears on the brink of dismissal, with Thomas Frank his most likely replacement.

Asked if he expected to remain in his job on the other side of the international break Sage said he deemed his prospects “better than you, I think”.

“We deserved better today,” the Frenchman said. “But football is not about what you deserve it is about how efficient you are and today we had a lack of efficiency”.

News.title: Lando Norris takes pole at Interlagos after chaotic qualifying session
News.content:
McLaren’s Lando Norris claimed pole for the São Paulo Grand Prix for a third consecutive year as he emerged victorious from a marathon, rain-affected qualifying session at Interlagos lasting two and a half hours.

But there was further frustration for his compatriot George Russell, who lashed out at his Mercedes pit wall after being told to abort a push lap in Q3 which he felt would have been good enough to finish qualifying in first place.

Whether Russell was right was debatable, but you could understand his frustration. The Briton has endured a miserable season, dropping from second to fourth in the drivers’ championship in Mexico last weekend after suffering yet another power unit issue.

Russell ended up leaving the Mexico paddock early while team-mate Kimi Antonelli celebrated becoming the sport’s youngest ever champion.

News.title: Man City look to be crumbling after guilty verdict
News.content:
Is this the day the xG gods reward Nottingham Forest? Oliver Glasner’s team sit 19th having won one game all season, but there is no doubt that their performances have been significantly better than results and they might need their luck to turn against Man City team full of firepower.

Despite all of the positive indicators in Forest’s underlying data, Glasner caused some alarm with his comments after last weekend’s defeat at Brentford.

The Austrian said: “We have to accept it’s not good enough. If we lose four of the last five games, it’s not good enough. And that’s why for me, it’s now time that we change things, that I change things, and that’s what I will do.

“I feel now maybe I made too many compromises in some stuff, and it’s always compromises. It’s a clear way. I will tell [the players] what we want to do, what we have to do, and if the players buy in, I think we can have a turnaround, and if not, the sixth manager [since the start of last season] will come in.”

Dangerous words perhaps when you work for Evangelos Marinakis, but John Percy reported this week that Glasner was backed by his players in a squad meeting.

City are smarting from back-to-back defeats by Aston Villa and Brighton, but they created more than enough in both games to claim some sort of result. Nevertheless, there is a persistent sense that their defensive unit remains too marshmellow-like over the course of 38 games, and Forest have the counter-attacking threat to test them.

Glasner has happy memories of playing City, beating them in the 2025 FA Cup final with Crystal Palace, but his Forest reign is in urgent need of a signature victory and performance.

Full team news on the way shortly.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick’s Man Utd contract ‘contains break clause’ which will save Red Devils fortune if they sack him
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED will reportedly not have to break the bank to sack Michael Carrick.

The Old Trafford legend, 45, is expected to be axed before the Red Devils return to action after the international break.



United are languishing in the Premier League’s relegation zone despite their dramatic injury-time comeback to notch a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday.

And, with just ONE win in ten games to start to the season, Old Trafford bigwigs are plotting a managerial change.



But talkSPORT reporter Ben Jacobs suggests United are set to save millions if they wield the axe.

Club legend Carrick had a one-year break clause included in his contract, making his dismissal more affordable.

United director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada are set to recommend a managerial change when they meet co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco on Tuesday.

And SunSport exclusively revealed potential successor Mauricio Pochettino would consider a Premier League return if the Red Devils come calling.

The former Tottenham chief saw his Old Trafford odds tumble from 25-1 to 2-1 second favourite in the wake of the stalemate with Villa.

And SunSport can reveal Pochettino, 54, is open to listening to an approach from the United hierarchy if Carrick is given the boot.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The Argentine guided the USA to the last-16 during the World Cup before crashing out against Belgium.

Pochettino has a release clause that could be triggered if he is pinpointed as United’s top target.

Carrick was rewarded with a two-year deal after spearheading the Red Devils to Champions League qualification last season.

But only one point is separating United from the foot of the Premier League table.



And skipper Bruno Fernandes sensationally blasted Carrick’s tactics during a bombshell interview last month.

United are the only side in the top-flight still searching for their second domestic win of the season.

Sports.title: Man City’s players are crumbling under the guilt of £1billion financial ‘sham’ – even footballers don’t live in a vacuum
Sports.content:
Next

THE clucking in the background sounds like Manchester City’s chickens coming home to roost.

Enzo Maresca was looking for crumbs of comfort on Saturday after his side crashed to their third successive Premier League defeat at Nottingham Forest.



But it is, surely, no real surprise City’s worst league run in two seasons comes as the initial internal sense of anger and indignation over the independent commission’s guilty verdict on the financial charges has been replaced by a realisation of what is hanging over the club.

Indeed, the last time they lost three on the bounce came two years ago — just as the hearing that eventually resulted in the ruling was getting started.



After all, City’s initial run of seven straight wins included two VAR calls in their favour.

First came the correct overturning of the initial stoppage-time offside flag against Josko Gvardiol in the opening weekend victory over Bournemouth.

And then, wrongly, allowing Erling Haaland’s Manchester derby winner to stand.

When — in the immediate aftermath of the findings of nearly £1billion in “sham” contracts, fired by determination to prove a point — City silenced the baying hordes of Anfield with a comprehensive 3-0 win, it looked like business as usual.

There were no obvious signs of a negative reaction inside the Etihad.

If anything, their resolve seemed even stronger.

A band of brothers, united against the world. Old-fashioned siege mentality.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Nothing at all wrong with that.

Yet for all the vehemence of the club’s response, the return of the inflatable bananas, the relishing of the fight and almost a revelling in the notoriety from the City faithful, Maresca’s players are only human.

While some travelling fans wore sky blue shirts with ‘Cheetos’ emblazoned across the front to taunt the Forest and other rival supporters, it was the City Ground that laughed last and longest.

And if, even in the smallest crevices of their minds, some of Maresca’s players start to wonder if anything they do this season will count, if an unprecedented sanction is already on the way, it is hard to imagine it will not have an impact on performances.

That does not diminish or negate City’s right to fight their corner. To appeal. To contest. To deploy their army of KCs in a legal skirmish.



It would, indeed, be bizarre, given the club’s position ever since the first batch of leaked emails in 2018, to expect anything less, especially now it is an existential fight.

But at the same time that stance has allowed some ludicrous positions to be taken by the City support base.

The idea the official anonymity of the three members of the independent commission is part of a conspiracy and evidence of collusion, is beyond laughable.

Lord Pannick and the rest of City’s legal team know who they are.

They did not sit behind a curtain for 42 days during the hearing to conceal their identities.



It is, indeed, almost certain — there are only so many leading silks — that they have previously appeared in courtrooms either in opposition or alongside the City KCs.

Quite possibly they are members of the same Pall Mall private clubs.

There is room for argument from both sides over the time elapsed from the start of the investigation, through the charges and hearing, to get to this point — and we still have not had the punishment or appeals.

Yet the notion that the “regrettable” — according to the commission — delay in coming to judgment is a sign of lack of faith in the verdict, what would they have said if the trio had rushed to judgment, committing to ten pages in a few days?

By the way, it WAS a verdict, by a quasi-legal three-man commission, with powers enshrined under the Arbitration Act 1996 and not, as City insisted, an “opinion”.



Some City fans have complained, too, about the confidentiality of the evidence-gathering and the “balance of probability” evidential proof required.

But the Law states arbitration processes MUST be conducted strictly in private.

The civil burden of proof, rather than the criminal “beyond reasonable doubt”, is also required.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Not that the City players are across any of that — but it is starting to look like they are feeling the effects of all of it.

Even footballers don’t exist inside a vacuum.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino would consider Premier League return with Man Utd with Michael Carrick on brink of Red Devils sack
Sports.content:
Next

MAURICIO POCHETTINO would consider a Prem return with Manchester United.

Former Spurs boss Poch saw his Old Trafford odds SLASHED from 25-1 to 2-1 second favourite in the wake of the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa that left United in the relegation zone.



And Sun Sport can reveal the Argentine, 54, is open to listening to an approach with the United hierarchy on the brink of sacking Michael Carrick.

Pochettino agreed a new four-year deal to stay at the helm of the US national side in the summer, following the success of their run to the World Cup last 16.



But Poch, whose main home is still in London, has never hidden his long-term desire to return to the Prem.

Just a couple of months ago he revealed he had received “some calls from different clubs” before the World Cup but that he had batted them away because of his commitment to the US.

Pochettino added: “Now we are thinking of spending four years with the USA but you can always break a contract, say you stop, and that’s it, you agree something.

“With a four-year contract, it’s different.

“We could lose Copa America or the Gold Cup, and they’re not happy with us, they can sack us, or we can say ‘ok it’s not in the way that we think’.”

Pochettino even suggested he would be interested in talking to the FA if they came calling, despite the rivalry with his homeland, adding: “For me we are very similar in the way we feel the passion of football.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“You respect all the things that I also grew up with in my country.”

He has long spoken of his admiration for United and the achievement of Sir Alex Ferguson and has been regularly linked with the Old Trafford role even during his time at Spurs.

United made a tentative approach when he was at PSG and then in 2022 Pochettino was edged out in a head to head with Erik ten Hag.

A year later, he was appointed at Chelsea but left Stamford Bridge after just one season following disputes with the Blues board.

Now though, he could be tempted to take charge of a third Prem club if United do want to offer him the chance.



Carrick has been clinging onto his job by a thread for weeks amid United’s dreadful form.

The club were initially set on dismissing the club legend after the 3-0 drubbing by Bournemouth two weeks ago.

But the lack of a succession plan and failure to settle on a replacement gave Carrick a stay of execution.



United have won one of their three games since — the comeback win over Roma in the Champions League — while tumbling to 18th and conceding eight goals.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And it is understood club bosses are finally ready to swing the axe during this week’s international break.

Old Trafford chiefs Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada are due to fly to Monaco to discuss future plans with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe on Tuesday.

Sports.title: Virgil van Dijk withdraws from Netherlands squad after Liverpool captain ‘played through pain in recent weeks’
Sports.content:
Next

LIVERPOOL captain Virgil Van Dijk has withdrawn from the Netherlands’ squad due to a knock after playing with a minor issue in recent weeks.

Holland are set for two crunch Nations League clashes against Greece at home on Friday and Germany away next Monday.



The national team issued an official statement revealing Van Dijk, 35, isn’t fit enough for the upcoming games.

According to The Athletic, the centre-back had been playing through pain these past few weeks for Liverpool.



The Oranje confirmed Sunderland star Brian Brobbey is unfit for the games with Greece and Jurgen Klopp‘s Germany as well.

The Netherlands also announced manager Xavi is not planning on calling up any replacements.



Van Dijk is only 35 caps away from beating Wesley Sneijder’s record of 134 appearances with the national team.

The Liverpool star and Brobbey aren’t the only big names forced to withdraw from international duty during this break.

Switzerland captain Granit Xhaka was ruled out after suffering a calf injury in the warm-up of Sunderland’s 1-0 win over Chelsea on Sunday.

The Swiss national team issued the following statement: “Granit Xhaka has to withdraw from the national team gathering due to a calf injury.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

And Arsenal prospect Ceadach O’Neill had to withdraw from Northern Ireland duty due to an injury of his own.

Manager Michael O’Neill said: “We’re naturally disappointed to be without Ceadach for the final two games of the campaign.

“He has been a great asset to the squad in the last international window and everyone here wishes him a swift recovery.”

Sports.title: Man Utd ‘to sack Michael Carrick’ as work begins on finding new boss after Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada’s crisis talks
Sports.content:
Next

MICHAEL CARRICK is on the brink of being axed by Manchester United.

The former midfielder, 45, was rewarded with a two-year deal after spearheading the Red Devils to Champions League qualification last season.



But, despite an late fightback to salvage a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday, United have gone into the international break sitting in the relegation zone.

And Old Trafford bigwigs are preparing to make a change in the dugout following the disastrous start to the season which has seen just ONE win in the Premier League this season.



The Athletic report United are set to sack Carrick after director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada held crunch talks.

Potential replacements are being identified and the Red Devils are expected to wield the axe before returning to action at Liverpool on November 22.



SunSport exclusively revealed on Monday that Mauricio Pochettino would consider a Premier League return with United.

The former Tottenham boss saw his Old Trafford odds tumble from 25-1 to 2-1 second favourite in the wake of the stalemate with Villa.

And SunSport can reveal the Argentine, 54, is open to listening to an approach from the United hierarchy if Carrick is given the boot.

Pochettino guided the USA to the last-16 during the World Cup before crashing out against Belgium.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The ex-Southampton supremo is ready to hold discussions with the Red Devils despite penning a contract extension a matter of months ago.

Wilcox and Berrada are planning to urge United co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe to axe Carrick when they meet in Monaco on Tuesday.

Old Trafford bigwigs initially planned to call time on his reign following the 3-0 thumping by Bournemouth two weeks ago.

But Carrick was given a stay of execution following conversations behind the scenes.



Key figures could not reach an agreement on a replacement, leading to no change being made.

Only one point separates United from the foot of the Premier League table.

Sports.title: Ex-England boss Sven-Goran Eriksson’s estate being chased for HUGE sum in unpaid tax by HMRC after coach’s passing
Sports.content:
Next

THE estate of former England football boss Sven-Goran Eriksson is being chased for £3.5million in unpaid tax.

HMRC officials have demanded the huge sum from the inheritance of the late Three Lions coach — who died of pancreatic cancer in August 2024, aged 76.



But his lawyer revealed last night there is no money left to settle the debt — apart from around £1million stashed in a Cayman Islands tax haven and £300,000 in a UK bank.

Anders Runebjer told The Sun: “Sven earned millions but was always too busy with his football and his ladies to manage money very well.



“I told the HMRC I’m not able to get the money in the Cayman Islands or his UK bank and said they’re welcome to seize it.

“They replied that they couldn’t do that so I told them there was nothing else left — so they won’t get paid.

“Sven was regularly sent bills by the British taxman and paid promptly but they changed the rules and now say he still owes £3.5million plus interest after he passed away.

“They’re welcome to take whatever they can get but I’m not giving them anything.”



Mr Runebjer said he would continue to work on behalf of Eriksson’s son Johan, 47, and 39-year-old daughter Lina to track down inheritance funds and investments.

He added: “My priority is trying to get whatever money I can that he left for his children — not the British taxman.”

Sven — who also managed Manchester City, Leicester City and Lazio — earned £25million while bossing the Three Lions from 2001 to 2006. But his “Golden Generation” featuring David Beckham and Steven Gerrard never won a trophy.

Swedish Sven was as famous for his flings with glamorous women as his tactical nous, cheating on long-term lover Nancy Dell’Olio with both TV star Ulrika Jonsson and FA secretary Faria Alam.

He died owing an estimated £7.25million and HMRC investigators are understood to be weighing up a legal move to claw back their share from the Caribbean haven.



A spokesman said: “We cannot comment on individuals.”

Sports.title: NFL legend Tom Brady quits Birmingham City despite Blues sitting top of Championship as club release statement
Sports.content:

TOM BRADY has quit Championship club Birmingham after just three years.

The Blues announced the NFL legend’s exit in a shock statement, with Brady‘s departure coming as they lead the Championship table.



Birmingham posted on X: “Birmingham City Football Club expresses its sincere gratitude to Tom Brady for his involvement with and unwavering support for the Club over the last three years.

“It was truly amazing to have someone with Tom’s experience and passion associated with the Club, and the Club looks forward to continuing to build on that foundation from the training ground to the Birmingham community.”



Beady partnered with Tom Wagner’s Knighthead Capital Management takeover back in July 2023.

This move came just one year after retiring from the NFL, having won seven Super Bowls with the New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Brady played a key role in the hedge fund’s plans to deliver Champions League football to the club, even being directly involved in transfer conversations.

These plans involve building a £3billion, 62,000-capacity stadium in the city.

It is one of several investments the legendary NFL quarterback has made, acquiring a 50 per cent stake in trading card business CardVault and backing virtual reality golf experience GOLF+.

Additionally, Brady purchased a five per cent stake in the NFL’s Las Vegas Raiders in 2024, joining Birmingham chief Wagner among the owners.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The Blues faced relegation from the Championship in their first season under Brady, before bouncing back with just three league losses during the 2023/24 campaign, even reaching the EFL Trophy final at Wembley.

Now the club leads the Championship after 15 matches, level on 19 points alongside Middlesbrough and Stoke, with their ambitions of reaching the Premier League edging closer to reality.

Now several Blues fans have come out to share their thanks to the ex-quarterback on social media.

One fan said: “Thank you for everything you’ve done for us Tom.”

Another shared: “NOOOOOO NOT THE GOAT. Thank you for everything Tom and come back for the promotion party at least.”



A third fan commented: “Thanks for everything Tom.”

Sports.title: Spain pay emotional tribute to Jesus de Miguel after Tenerife striker’s tragic death colliding with goalkeeper
Sports.content:
Next

SPAIN paid an emotional tribute to Tenerife’s late star Jesus de Miguel after his tragic death on the pitch before the world champions’ first training session ahead of their clash with England.

De Miguel passed away at the age of 30 after a freak collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during last week’s Spanish Segunda Division game at the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez Stadium.



Owono, 25, was sent off in the closing stages of the second half when his knee collided with the striker’s head and chest as he rushed out to clear a long ball during a counter-attack with the score at 2-2.

The forward was left motionless after the impact and medics rushed to the pitch as players wept before the referee abandoned the match in the seventh minute of stoppage time.



According to Marca, De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest on his way to hospital and was resuscitated by paramedics.

The Madrid native was admitted to intensive care, where his condition was described as “stable but serious” by Tenerife that same night.



But tragedy struck as his health deteriorated and he was pronounced dead the following morning.

Tributes have been pouring from fans, players and clubs from around the world throughout the entirety of last week.

And Spain followed suit by honouring their compatriot with a touching gesture during their first training session in Madrid as they gear up for the international break.

Unai Simon and Ferran Torres – accompanied by the world champions’ manager Luis de la Fuente – left a shirt and a bouquet of flowers in the centre circle.



The whole team then gathered in the middle of the pitch and observed a minute’s silence along with staff and a handful of fans.

This comes after heartbroken Tenerife supporters gathered around their home stadium, where the incident took place, to honour their beloved player with flowers, candles and emotional letters.

Spain are set to visit the Czech Republic on Thursday before hosting England on Sunday in the Nations League.

Sports.title: Carrick position increasingly in doubt as hierarchy mulls over his future
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick's position as Manchester United head coach is looking increasingly in doubt, but Sky Sports News has been told as yet, no final decision has been taken about his future.

As reported earlier on Monday, the club is carrying out a full review of the team's performance so far this season, led by director of football Jason Wilcox, with a plan for a decision to be made before the end of this international break.

Carrick was given a reprieve following the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth a fortnight ago, with the bosses keen to give him a further three matches to try to turn the team's fortunes around.

But the pressure has continued to mount on Carrick after an eighth straight Premier League match without a win. There are now real doubts about whether he will be in charge of the team which goes to Anfield to play Liverpool the weekend after next.

The United hierarchy is determined that results have to improve, but they want to be sure about which direction to take the team before any action is taken.

If they decide to remove Carrick from his position, they want to avoid having an interim head coach take over, but as yet, there have been no substantive talks with other potential candidates.

Sky Sports News understands the club's hierarchy are planning to use the international break to fully evaluate the season so far and reassess their options.

Carrick and the players have all had Monday off after rescuing a late point against Villa on Sunday, but the head coach and his staff are due back into Carrington on Tuesday.

With most players away on international duty and no first-team training sessions planned in the coming days, that has bought some breathing space for a full re-evaluation of the season.

One win in 11 games, 30 goals conceded so far in all competitions, the worst record of any team in the top-five European leagues, and a worst-ever start to a Premier League season has ramped up the pressure on Carrick.

Those problems have outweighed the positivity brought about by the comebacks of the last two matches.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Adam Binnie shares six stats that show Manchester United's troubles so far this season

It is thought the United hierarchy feel Carrick over-achieved last season, with a third-placed League finish earning Champions League football.

But it is equally clear the bosses are adamant that the club's current crop of players have woefully under-achieved so far this season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Manchester United fans show their love for Michael Carrick at full-time with a rendition of 'It's Carrick you know, it's hard to believe it's not Scholes' after the Red Devils fight back to draw 4-4 with Aston Villa at Old Trafford

Sky Sports News understands there are three key reasons why United are not rushing a decision over the head coach position - all of which have given Carrick an extended stay of execution.

Firstly, the supporters are not singing for him to be sacked. It is unlikely that will ever happen, such is the affection of the fanbase for a legendary player who won 11 major trophies with United, including the Champions League and five Premier League titles.

As such, the pressure to change the boss which other clubs often experience from the stands has not materialised at Old Trafford.

Secondly, there is a feeling in the boardroom that Carrick and his coaching staff still retain the support of the players.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Manchester United and Aston Villa

Despite the chaotic nature of the last two games, they have produced a Champions League win against Roma and a draw against a good Villa side - with notable comebacks in both.

As such, the assessment seems to be that the players have not downed tools, and they are still fighting for Carrick.

Thirdly, United's bosses remain unconvinced at this stage that changing the head coach will solve the team's problems.

If they did believe that, they could have already made a move to sack Carrick and appoint a candidate such as Julian Nagelsmann or Eddie Howe - both of whom are out of work, available, and thought to be keen to talk to United if a vacancy becomes available.

'It doesn't matter who's in charge at Man Utd'

Sky Sports News chief reporter Kaveh Solhekol:

"The club needs to become Manchester United again. They need to turn into a club who are capable of winning the title regularly, winning the European Cup again.

"It doesn't matter who's in charge, in my opinion. You could have Carlo Ancelotti, Pep Guardiola or Jurgen Klopp. But with the present ownership structure, I don't think things are going to change.

"You could bring in another manager but you would just paper over the cracks. We're talking about a club that used to rub shoulders with Barcelona and Real Madrid.

"If things carry on as they are at the moment, they'll be rubbing shoulders with Lincoln and QPR. There's a circus around the club, everyone talking about what's going wrong and how it can be changed.

"But I think most Man Utd fans think that unless you change the owners, nothing is going to change."

Sports.title: Sabalenka starts pursuit of WTA Finals title with opening win
Sports.content:
Aryna Sabalenka got off to a winning start at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells, battling past Karolina Muchova 7-6 (7-2) 7-5, while Mirra Andreeva was also victorious in her Group 2 opener on Monday.

A two-time beaten finalist in the WTA Finals - including going down last year to Elena Rybakina, who stole her No 1 ranking this season - Sabalenka is looking to win the tournament for the first time.

Rybakina's late withdrawal due to a viral illness and fatigue aids Sabalenka's hopes, as does her opening victory over Wimbledon finalist Muchova, who made her sweat for it in a hugely-absorbing contest that ran six minutes shy of two hours.

Image: Aryna Sabalenka is looking to win the season-ending WTA Finals for the first time

Sabalenka was first to blink on serve in the first set, Muchova breaking for a 3-2 advantage, and again to lead 5-4, only for her opponent to break back immediately on both occasions - the second time when the Czech world No 7 was serving to take the opener.

Sabalenka then spurned a couple of set points in Muchova's next service game, but dominated the resulting tiebreaker, dropping just two points.

The second set followed a similar pattern to the first, though it was Sabalenka this time who was twice pegged back from going a break to the good, before the four-time Grand Slam champion claimed the decisive break of serve to lead 6-5 before serving things out and clinching victory on her second match point.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aryna Sabalenka was thrilled after beating Karolina Muchova in straight sets in her opening match at the WTA Finals.

"It was a tough battle, it's always tough matches against her," Sabalenka told Sky Sports afterwards. "She's such a high IQ player and every time you have to be focussed, ready for everything and have to play smart.

"I'm super happy I was able to start with a win."

Andreeva makes light work of Svitolina

World No 3 Andreeva, who won her first Grand Slam at the French Open earlier this year, enjoyed a much more routine win to start her tournament as she eased past Elina Svitolina 6-4 6-0.

It was a near faultless performance from the 19-year-old as she wrapped up victory in 71 minutes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Mirra Andreeva against Elina Svitolina from the WTA Finals.

After saving a break point in her second service game, Svitolina couldn't hold off Andreeva in her next as she earned three more at 0-40 - converting the first for a 3-2 advantage she would not relinquish.

The second set was even more straightforward as Andreeva didn't drop a single game against the world No 6, albeit she did have to stave off four break points when serving the match out.

Much attention is focused on Andreeva this week after Jessica Pegula labelled her a "diva" who "needs to be humbled" during a conversation with her coach that was picked up on a hot mic in a practice session at Indian Wells.

The WTA apologised for failing to properly inform players about active microphones, with chair Valerie Camillo saying there was "a lack of advanced notice and clear signage" as she confirmed audio will now be switched off for practice sessions.

Speaking to Sky Sports, Andreeva said she struggled on court despite the impressive nature of her opening win: "I don't remember myself being so nervous on the court," she said.

"I felt like my legs were shaking. It was extremely tough, so I'm super happy to get through the match.

"My main goal today was to try to block out all of the thoughts and the emotions, force myself to move like supersonic, but it felt completely the opposite - I felt like an elephant."

Andreeva added: "After this match, after feeling so many nerves, I think it's going to give me more confidence knowing I can get through."

Pegula is in Group 1, along with Coco Gauff, Linda Noskova and Martya Kostyuk, who all got their tournaments under way on Sunday, with Pegula beaten in her opening match against fellow American Gauff.

Sports.title: Ballon d'Or winner Kane not named in FIFPRO World 11
Sports.content:
Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane has not been named in the FIFPRO World 11.

Over 18,000 professional footballers have chosen their best men's team, with the final 11 being chosen from a group of 26 selected finalists.

Kane, who won the Ballon d'Or ahead of Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe by one of the smallest margins in history, was among the 26 finalists but did not make the final team.

Mbappe, Manchester City's Erling Haaland, Barcelona's Lamine Yamal and Inter Miami's Lionel Messi were named in a Kane-less front four, which also excluded Cristiano Ronaldo and Michael Olise.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Harry Kane admits winning this year's Ballon d'Or was 'beyond his wildest dreams' and says he's happy to put England 'back on the map' by being the first Englishman to win the trophy in 25 years

Kane became the first English Ballon d'Or winner last month since Michael Owen in 2001, and only the fifth in history following in the footsteps Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Owen.

The Bayern Munich star received just 27.6 per cent of votes of all the forwards, with Haaland marginally bettering him at 28.4 per cent. It is the first time since the award's inception in 2005 that the Ballon d'Or winner has not been selected for the XI.

Kane's international team-mate, Jude Bellingham, was named in midfield alongside Barcelona star Rodri and PSG's Vitinha.

Arsenal's David Raya was named in goal, with Pau Cubarsi, Achraf Hakimi and Nuno Mendes rounding things out in a back three.

Sports.title: Grand Slam of Darts 2026: Littler alongside Greaves in mouth-watering Group A
Sports.content:
Luke Littler has been drawn in Group A alongside Beau Greaves and Niels Zonneveld at the Grand Slam of Darts 2026; you can watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports from November 14-22

Grand Slam of Darts 2026: Luke Littler grouped with Beau Greaves as he looks to defend title in Wolverhampton

Highlights of last year's Grand Slam of Darts final clash between Luke Littler and Luke Humphries

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

The draw for the Grand Slam of Darts 2026 has taken place with Luke Littler grouped alongside Beau Greaves and Niels Zonneveld to make a mouth-watering Group A.

Littler and Greaves have faced each other twice before, with each young star picking up a victory and they will once again face-off in the evening session on Saturday November 14.

Sports.title: England duo ruled out of rest of Nations Championship
Sports.content:
England will be without Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and Tom Curry for the remainder of their Nations Championship campaign after both players were ruled out due to injury.

It comes as Steve Borthwick's side has been hit with a series of injuries ahead of their clash against Japan on Saturday.

Seb Atkinson, who came off in the second-half of England's 45-22 win against Australia, is set to miss the match with a hip injury, along with Ollie Chessum (shoulder) and George Furbank (groin).

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Maro Itoje gave a passionate defence of Steve Borthwick after England's victory over Australia at Twickenham

England are optimistic the trio will be available for their clash against New Zealand at Allianz Stadium on Saturday, November 21.

Feyi-Waboso sustained an injury to his right ankle during the first-half of England's clash against the Wallabies, following a hip-drop tackle by Australia prop Angus Bell.

Bell was later sent to the sin bin, with Henry Pollock coming on to replace Feyi-Waboso on the wing at half-time. Pollock would go on to score twice.

The Exeter winger's absence could see Borthwick call on Saracens fliers Noah Caluori or Tobias Elliott for England's clash against Japan.

Image: Tom Curry missed England's clash against Australia due to a hip injury he sustained in training

It would be Caluori's third cap for England, having made his senior debut during their Nations Championship clash against Fiji in July.

Centres Joe Marchant and Will Joseph could also be considered as wing options, while Fraser Dingwall or Max Ojomoh are likely to take the No 12 jersey in place of Atkinson.

Curry did not feature in England's win over Australia after he sustained a hip injury during training last week.

Borthwick revealed after Sunday's win that his brother, Ben Curry, was unlikely to start against Japan, despite the openside enjoying an excellent outing against the Wallabies.

It is likely Borthwick could deploy Freddie Steward at full-back in place of Furbank and keep Marcus Smith on the bench as utility cover.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Steve Borthwick praised 'excellent' Henry Pollock after a standout performance on the wing for England against Australia

England's 36-player squad returned to Pennyhill Park on Monday to prepare for this weekend's clash, with Jack Kenningham and Max Hicks both being drafted into the squad as back-row cover for Ben Curry and Chessum.

Meanwhile, Archie McParland has returned to the training squad after recovering from a calf injury.

Sports.title: Dubois: I'm the biggest test for Baumgardner's career
Sports.content:
Caroline Dubois is confident she is one fight away from an undisputed showdown with her American rival Alycia Baumgardner.

Baumgardner, formerly an undisputed super-featherweight champion, moved up to lightweight to dominate Elif Nur Turhan and win the IBF lightweight world title.

In El Paso on February 20, live on Sky Sports, Dubois fights Stephanie Han, looking to add the WBA championship to the WBO and WBC lightweight titles she already holds.

She was in Texas on Sunday, to face off with Han and call out Baumgardner.

As much as there is enmity between Dubois and Baumgardner, who have now had a number of fierce confrontations, the Londoner was pleased to see her rival step up to the 135lb division.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the fight between Turhan and Baumgardner

"Of course, I knew it was going to happen. I said it. I said that there was nothing left for her at 130," Dubois told Sky Sports. "She's been a position now where she's run out of opponents.

"You have to challenge yourself, you have to test yourself and that test, the biggest test for her career is going to be against me. I knew she was going to have to step up."

To stay on track herself, Dubois must defeat Han in February. Han is unbeaten as a professional and has two high-profile wins on her ledger over Holly Holm as well. But Dubois is determined to overcome her in her hometown and move on.

She insists she will not back down from Baumgardner. She does not want the American to equivocate either.

"What's the point of moving up in weight and having one belt? There's no point going halfway, you go all the way. When you're on a quest for greatness, you go all the way," Dubois said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the lightweight fight between Dubois and Amelia Moore

"I know for myself, I want to be undisputed. I'll be very frustrated if I fight and unify as much as I can and there's just one belt and she's terrified to step in the ring me and prevents me from becoming undisputed. I think that would be a whack move and I would be very disappointed."

But Dubois added: "If she's as great as she says she is then hopefully that's the character she will have and she would relish the opportunity.

"It's something that we both have to work towards, to make sure when the fight happens it's on the biggest platform, the biggest stage and we're given the respect we deserve for putting ourselves on the line."

Watch Dubois vs Han on February 20 live on Sky Sports.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick facing Manchester United axe amid review by Jason Wilcox
Sports.content:
Manchester United are moving towards sacking Michael Carrick, though no final decision has been made by Jason Wilcox, the director of football, who is leading the review after the head coach was given the Chelsea, Roma and Aston Villa games to turn results around.

Wilcox has been consulting with Omar Berrada, the chief executive, before a recommendation regarding Carrick is made to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, who controls sporting policy.

If Carrick is removed, Mauricio Pochettino has emerged as a potential candidate as it is understood the USA head coach is open to the position, while sources indicate that Eddie Howe also remains on the radar of Wilcox too.

The former Newcastle manager is taking a break from the game but would consider the job if offered it. United are in the Premier League relegation zone and have three victories in 15 games in all competitions. Carrick came close to being removed after the 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth on 25 October. But after Wilcox and Berrada met the following day at the training ground to discuss his position, Carrick was given the three games until the international break to prove he and the players could reverse a dismal start.

A defeat, a win and a draw in those matches plus the team’s displays in each compounded with the overall run of form has moved Wilcox and Berrada towards a position where they are minded to remove Carrick. There is a growing expectation within the club that he will lose his job.

The final decision is yet to be made, though. When contacted on Monday night by the Guardian the club declined to comment.

In what may prove Carrick’s final three games in charge, United lost 2-0 at Chelsea, beat Roma 3-2 at Old Trafford and drew 4-4 at home against Villa on Sunday. In each game United were uneven. At Chelsea, Carrick’s side impressed in the first half but failed to convert chances before conceding twice after the interval, the second from a penalty after Lisandro Martínez was sent off.

In the Roma victory they were 2-0 behind in a poor opening 45 minutes before three goals in a rousing second one. On Sunday United twice trailed by two goals and entered added time 4-2 down, strikes from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu rescuing a point.

After the Roma game Carrick urged his team to build momentum but within four minutes against Villa they were 2-0 down, continuing a pattern of conceding very early. In the 4-1 defeat at Como> last month, Nico Paz scored after two minutes. This followed Pablo Barrios’s opener one minute into the 2-0 defeat at Atlético Madrid> the previous week.

Sports.title: Manchester’s soulless content machine football clubs sum up post-imperial Britain | Barney Ronay
Sports.content:
In Manchester this weekend it was possible to bookend your Thursday‑to‑Sunday entertainment with two cultural events. First up, a debut screening of the re‑released and uncensored Ken Russell film The Devils at Trafford Odeon. And three days later, three miles down the road, Manchester United versus Aston Villa at Old Trafford.

As expected, one of these events provided a visceral cinematic experience, a deeply disturbing two-hour public meditation on the meaning of faith, blood, fear, power, ritual and the fetishising of objects, climaxing in an orgiastic crowd scene of depraved but undeniably erotic abandon, all acted out on a set in a state of glorious and performative ruin. And the other one was a film with Oliver Reed in it.

By the final whistle that wild 4‑4 draw at Old Trafford felt like a fitting endpoint to the opening quarter of the Premier League season. As we head into a 12‑day international break it is customary at this point to take a set of readings, to anatomise the season to date, to offer up a state of the Premier League address.

Five games since the last time we did this, not a great deal has changed. Brighton have maintained their luminous insurgent energy. The headline chart-breakers are Tottenham, up from second‑bottom to 11th. The official Home Office Spurs In Crisis threat level has been downgraded from Definitely In Crisis to Probably In Crisis A Bit Later On. Roberto De Zerbi no longer looks like a doomed and haunted cartoon caterpillar. Instead he looks like a feisty and fun haunted cartoon caterpillar.

Otherwise there has been only one story in town across that autumn segment. And that story is Manchester, and the extraordinary contortions of two contrasting, but deeply conjoined mega-clubs.

Manchester City’s run from October to November kicked off with the guilty verdict on almost all of their financial charges, followed by an adrenal victory at Anfield, and finally a run of three problematic league defeats. United have basically fallen through the floor in the same period: played eight in all comps, won one, and a point off the bottom of the Premier League table.

At the same time both Manchester clubs have dominated the news cycle, inexhaustible content machines, and the source of football-adjacent stories so strange and so vast they threaten to surge up over the seawall and consume the rest of the league.

It is necessary at this point to talk about Michael Carrick and whether he has been sacked yet (current answer: no). It seems likely that this will happen in the current break, once the designated replacement has been lined up. Another Manchester United paradox: only here, in the realm of the mid-season panic-sacking do we suddenly feel ourselves in the hands of a slick and well-practised machine. Stand aside. We’re old hands at this. Leave it to the experts.

View image in fullscreen Manchester United fans stage a protest before the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday. Photograph: Conor Molloy/ProSports/Shutterstock

But Carrick is of course essentially another bystander to the ongoing reactor core meltdown. He didn’t appoint Michael Carrick. He has done nothing surprising in his role as head coach, simply been the best Michael Carrick he can be, which is a Michael Carrick unqualified for this level of management.

Even the club executives captured by the TV pictures in insinuating close-up every week are essentially bit-part players, useful idiots for the regime: the director of football, Jason Wilcox, who looks every week a bit more like an office clerk trapped inside a hijacked foreign embassy trying to signal desperately with his eyes that he’s close to the edge and can someone in a flak jacket please appear at the fire escape window pretty soon. And the chief executive, Omar Berrada, who personally oversaw the Manchester City commercial sponsorship regime, and surely can’t be allowed to stay in his role at a listed company if the appeal against City’s charges is dismissed.

These are just the visible symptoms, not the cause. This is what happens when you run an institution where it is necessary to appoint people at significant levels who are willing to exist at a compromised level, who feel delighted to have the chance to run this organisation, even badly.

And by now it feels too easy to say the obvious thing. Manchester United have one competent but entirely self-motivated majority owner, for whom this has been a wonderful financial opportunity; and another owner whose only addition to the spectacle is to demonstrate the non‑transferable skills of the average billionaire.

We know this now. United are trapped in a cycle of self‑consumption. It is an ingrained, self-cannibalising decline, like a depressed post‑industrialised city in miniature. All that remains is rust, people and unspent heritage.

But it has also created something extraordinary in the past few weeks. Right now the Old Trafford match‑day atmosphere feels entirely unlike anything else, not just in sport but any other human activity at which you care to point.

View image in fullscreen Roberto De Zerbi no longer looks like a doomed and haunted cartoon caterpillar. Instead he looks like a feisty and fun haunted cartoon caterpillar. Photograph: Scott Heppell/Reuters

The periphery is now enshrined definitively as The Event. Here is a man in sodden navy woollen menswear haunted by strange noises, striding the touchline like King Lear on his way to a golfing weekend. Here is the United crowd clamped together inside a clanky and leaking stadium, gripped by macro‑forces, shouting at the tides of power, a drama of alienation taking place just beyond the white lights around the lip of the stand.

The currents of energy are so mixed and nuanced. Who is cheering what? Where exactly is the love, the fear, the rage directed at this moment? Like all the best human dramas it is both sweeping and bathetic, thousands of human souls in that same shared space, all focused on an abstract idea, the act of faith and memory they identify collectively as Manchester United, while in front of them Harry Maguire trots about like an ageing police horse and Diogo Dalot attempts to play football with his legs on the wrong way round.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

To the unconverted, football can seem like a distraction, a silly thing, the society of the spectacle with the society part aggressively deleted. But there is still something noble about howling into this physical space, about expressing dissent, protest, rage, which is the opposite of so many things that are unsatisfying about the wider world: fakery, remote emotion, remote experience.

Take a look at the world that surrounds the team on the pitch: asset-stripping owners, branding overload, a club that is entirely committed to monetising your emotions. To rage at this thing is not just rational and human but an appropriate act of resistance.

This is where the autumn 2026 version of Manchester City also enters the picture. On the pitch City were muddled and unusually open in midfield during the 3-1 defeat by an excellent Nottingham Forest on Saturday. But something has changed around the club in this period, expressed most powerfully in that travelling support.

The urge to defy the independent tribunal verdict, to lean into being “villains”, has been a little baffling from the outside. It is hard to understand how truth, freedom, sunlight, the little man kicking against the pricks is compatible with swallowing the party line of an autocratic propaganda project.

But the space is more complex than that, the tension less linear. The City fans in Cheetos shirts waving inflatable mnemonic bananas, raising their fists to the world, have also become strangely captivating, persuasive, unexpectedly likeable.

View image in fullscreen The Manchester clubs feel in their separate ways like a version of their own city’s modern form. Photograph: Michael Zemanek/Shutterstock

Because this is also at bottom a protest against a world that feels beyond your reach. Forget the accounting regulation stuff and it isn’t hard to find plenty that is cheerless in the Premier League model, in the complete prostration of elite football at the altar of money. Whatever its source, no matter how muddled the logic, there is a base‑level majesty in this spectacle of defiance and collectivism.

If it feels addictive, moreish, impossible to look away from, then maybe this is because something authentic is happening in a world of fakery and illusions. The Manchester clubs feel in their separate ways like a version of their own city’s modern form, of the way post‑post‑imperial Britain has tried to create energy from inward investment or stripping its parts, selling its soul for some glass and steel high-rises and a tramline. It is a process that also includes turning supporters of a football club into product, a piece of staging, the trees on an architects drawing.

There is no obvious solution to this, no way of reversing that process given the selling off of land, control, intellectual property, just as it can seem like there is no obvious practical route towards the soft, comforting, previously attainable things Andy Burnham conjures up in his speeches about the future.

But it is interesting to see football directly confronting this alienation, expressing, however incoherently, that the only sensible response is a refusal to be silent. The Premier League is in its own way a perfect reflection of the nation, with its ailing but wealthy boomer generation, its lightweight pop-up entities filling the vacant spaces in the high street.

The other key story of the autumn period is of course Arsenal, who are basically London in the form of a football club, economically functional, geographically privileged, ticking along under its carefully curated restrictions. Is this the story of the season from here? Even with 28 games still to play it is hard to see Arsenal’s five‑point lead as anything other than a steady progression towards another league title.

At the same time every metric, from social media spikes to estimated TV figures, suggests that the event of the weekend was by some distance a theatrical but essentially meaningless 4-4 draw in the rain on Sunday night. Drink it in. Raise a fist to the world. Manchester has been the capital of English football for so long. It remains, even in a state of football‑adjacent crisis, its most potent spectacle, still able to provide a sense of something real in a post-real world.

Sports.title: Ben White says he has no complaints at boos from England fans over self-imposed exile
Sports.content:
Ben White has said he has no complaints at being booed by England fans when he ended his international exile during the 1-1 draw with ­Uruguay this year.

The Arsenal defender, who has returned to Thomas Tuchel’s squad after missing last month’s camp because of injury, became unpopular with some supporters after leaving the 2022 World Cup in Qatar early for personal reasons. White made himself unavailable for the rest of Gareth Southgate’s time in charge and was given a frosty reception from the Wembley crowd when he came off the bench to make his first England appearance in almost four years during the friendly with Uruguay last March.

“Everyone can do whatever they want,” White told BBC 5 Live as he prepared for England’s Nations League games against Croatia and Spain this week. “It’s fine with me. Whatever they want to do, and I think just think about maybe not knowing the full story. And if they did, maybe they wouldn’t.”

Tuchel has ignored the negative reaction. The England manager wants to work with White, who followed scoring the opening goal against Uruguay by giving away a late penalty for the equaliser.

“Before the game I was thinking: ‘Don’t not stand out, but just nice and easy,’” White said. “Then I came on and obviously get booed. Then I score. Then I give away a pen. It was obviously full of emotions that night, and it was a good night.”

White, who has been in fine form for Arsenal this season, continues to steer clear of giving his take on the events leading to his exit from Qatar. “A load’s been said,” he said. “I’ve probably seen all of it and I think people don’t know the full story because I’ve never said anything and won’t put anyone under the bus or share any of that. I think it’s probably the best way. Obviously a bit tricky and not straightforward, but it’s amazing to be here now.”

The 29-year-old does not think he would have done anything differently. “I don’t think I would,” White said. “I was a bit younger. I’m a bit older now. As a person I’m quite real, and I think I made the decision that I would probably continue to make. One that I’m not happy about but it happened. It’s time to move on.”

Tuchel’s hopes of taking White to the World Cup last summer were dashed by a knee injury at the end of last season. White, who can play at right-back and in central defence, would probably have been part of the squad and he told TalkSport he cried when he realised he was out of contention. Injuries have disrupted his progress in recent years but he has made 12 appearances for Arsenal this season and he hopes to earn a place at Euro 2028.

“I’ve been obviously around it and not quite put my foot in the door in these big games,” White said. “It’s definitely something I want to do and be involved in.”

Tuchel did not have to work hard to persuade him to return to the England fold, he said: “The boss didn’t need to say too much. The effort he made to speak to me and reach out was so nice, and I really appreciated it. I think when you see a manager like that you want to learn from him. It was a huge thing to play for Thomas.”

Dan Burn has been called into the squad after Marc Guéhi withdrew with an injury.

Sports.title: Manchester City’s weaknesses under Enzo Maresca are being exposed
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca seemed, if not quite baffled by his side’s Saturday defeat to Nottingham Forest, then at least a little put out. After seven straight wins from the start of the season, that’s now three straight defeats, a pattern so unusual that it’s been recorded only once before in top-flight English history, by Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05. The three defeats were all different, Maresca said, although in all of them City had had more possession and more chances.

In the 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa two weeks ago, City had 63% of the ball and had 15 chances to Villa’s eight. In the 1-0 home defeat to Brighton last weekend, they had 62% possession and 21 chances to seven. At the City Ground, it was 79% possession and 12 chances to 11. So Maresca is right in one way: City could look at basic statistics and say they had been unfortunate – although Forest could equally point to the fact that they went into that game third top of the expected goals table but second-bottom of the actual table.

But there is another statistic that should concern Maresca: City have not kept a clean sheet since their victory at Anfield after the last international break, nine games ago. And the game before that, they let in three against Sunderland. In those last eight games, City have conceded 17 goals. It’s true that three of those can at least in part be blamed on errors by Gianluigi Donnarumma, but there are also structural issues. City have a vulnerability in transition that Forest ruthlessly exploited, a weakness not unfamiliar to Maresca’s teams. One of the criticisms he received at both Leicester and Chelsea was that his sides were often extremely cautious in possession, but that makes sense given how high a line he likes to play.

That’s also why duels are so crucial to his teams; losing possession immediately exposes a high back four. Maresca was visibly disappointed at the way City were outfought in the first half against Forest. Lose the ball and the opposition has a run at a back four with space behind it. That is always going to be a problem but especially so when the opposing center-forward is a Liam Delap who has just remembered how to play and is determined to make somebody pay for a year and a bit of disappointing form.

Yet the midfield Maresca picked was clearly vulnerable to being outmuscled. He clearly rates Enzo Fernández extremely highly, to the point that City paid £125m ($167.7m) to sign him from Chelsea. But Fernández, for all his gifts as a footballer, is not especially physical by the standards of the Premier League. When he and Cole Palmer played together, there was often a sense that it made Chelsea a little lightweight. Maresca, though, was so determined to field the Argentinian that he would come up with complex tactical solutions, such as using Malo Gusto as a weird right-back-cum-No-10 hybrid.

City are running into similar problems. Rayan Cherki is an enormously gifted attacking midfielder, but not one who can be relied upon defensively, either in terms of his positioning or his willingness to make tracking runs, something Pep Guardiola acknowledged last season. He can be physically outmatched. That is not necessarily a huge problem with two mobile runners behind him: ideally an Elliot Anderson-style shuttler and a more defensive holding and/or ball-winning presence like Rodri. But Rodri has gone and Fernández leaves Anderson with a huge amount of the physical work to do. If Anderson happens not to be on the spot – if, say, a defender loses the ball in a dangerous area, or a break bypasses him – City are very quickly exposed.

Maresca said he will use this international break to reassess, that this was a rare example where it was better for a team not to have another game straight away to try to put a defeat behind them. Perhaps there is a tactical solution to be found. Perhaps even one that isn’t just: don’t play Fernández and Cherki together. But he must also be aware that by the time the Premier League returns, City could be out of the title race, or effectively even out of the Premier League itself.

It was during the last international break that the independent panel announced City had been found guilty of all but one of the charges brought against them by the Premier League. There is a school of thought that the sanctions could be announced during this international break. It’s all but impossible, of course, to know precisely how it’s affecting players to play under the cloud of a potential huge points deduction, but if initial defiance has faded into a sullen acceptance, that may also lead to battles being lost, to a lack of intensity and desire.
