World.title: Verdict delayed in Honduras sex-trafficking case linked to disappearance
World.content:
A court in Honduras has delayed a verdict in a sex-trafficking case linked to the 2022 disappearance of Angie Pena, a case that has raised concerns about impunity in transnational crimes.

On Monday, Honduras’s judiciary cited the need to review evidence and wait for the return of a court interpreter, who was out of the country. The decision has been delayed until November 20.

The verdict was expected that same day. Critics framed the unexpected delay as yet another hurdle in a case that has drawn comparisons to the crimes of the late Jeffrey Epstein, a convicted sex offender in the US accused of running a sex-trafficking ring.

Four men, including two US citizens, are on trial for crimes related to Pena’s disappearance four years ago.

Harold Green and William James Murdock, both from the US, face human-trafficking charges. Another US citizen, Gary Lee Johnston, and Honduran citizen Gustavo Trejo are accused of criminal association.

Honduran authorities have also sought an Interpol notice for another suspect, US citizen Antony Frank Grayson.

The Honduran public prosecutor’s office said the suspects are part of a network involved in crimes including drug trafficking and sex trafficking involving minors.

It alleges police and at least one judge helped facilitate the criminal network, without naming the officials.

Defence lawyers, however, have denied the men’s involvement and requested an acquittal.

Pena went missing on January 1, 2022, after setting out on a jet ski from West Bay on the Honduran island of Roatan, while vacationing with her family.



Authorities initially focused on a rescue mission at sea, treating her disappearance as a possible accident.

But the case expanded into a trafficking investigation after Pena’s jet ski was found in Belize, some 170km (90 nautical miles) away.

In August 2022, authorities investigating the disappearance found a minor in the Roatan house occupied by Johnston, who was later sentenced to 32 years for commercial sex trafficking and child pornography in a separate case.

An analysis by Honduran media found that the country was mentioned more than 100 times in the Epstein files, including multiple references to Roatan, from where Pena disappeared.

“There are many more women and girls who have been victims of trafficking networks, and those cases are silenced, they go unpunished,” said Kenia Paz, a lawyer for the Legal Team for Human Rights, which represents Pena’s family.

Lawyers representing the family have questioned the lack of transparency in the investigation and in the trial, which was not open to the press or the general public.

Postponing the verdict “fuels the perception of impunity, increases public distrust in state security institutions, and prolongs the suffering and vulnerability of affected families”, said former Honduran Vice Minister of Security Julissa Villanueva in a post on X.

Dereck McNeil, a key protected witness, was killed in August, spurring further concerns about the case.

In videos made public after his death, McNeil alleged corruption within a special unit of the public prosecutor’s office known as the ATIC.

He accused the unit of leaking information about the case and being linked to drug-trafficking networks.

The ATIC director has denied any corruption and said that the unit has not been involved in investigating Pena’s disappearance.

Villanueva, the former vice minister, told The Associated Press that she believes prosecutors mishandled the case from the start, pushing a “tunnel vision” explanation of what happened.

“There are connections with other larger networks, and only by making them public will this family be able to get justice,” said Villanueva.

“It’s not just Angie. It’s all those women around Angie. There are many.”

World.title: Trump says FBI investigating Nvidia boss's affair with alleged Chinese spy
World.content:
US President Donald Trump has said the FBI is investigating the affair between the chief executive of Nvidia and an alleged Chinese spy.

Trump said he spoke to Jensen Huang on Monday following reports that the US believed he had been targeted in a Chinese espionage campaign.

"I asked him that question, 'Did you have any idea she was a spy?' He said 'I had no idea she was a spy' and I really believe him," Trump told reporters.

Beijing has rejected claims that Huang was targeted, with its foreign ministry saying the allegations were "entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China".

Nvidia, which has commissioned an independent investigation into the affair involving Alice Huang, alleged to be a Chinese spy, said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised.

Nvidia is the world's second most valuable company after Apple, and designs computer chips that have become central to AI technology. The revelations knocked about $250bn (Â£190bn) off its value on Monday as the company's share price fell by more than 4%.

Trump later told reporters at the White House that the FBI was looking into the issue, but did not elaborate on the investigation, or when it was launched. The FBI declined to comment when contacted by the BBC.

US intelligence officials believe Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was a spy for Beijing, according to a New York Times report. She is not related to Jensen Huang.

According to the newspaper, Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to top officials in Washington last spring, warning that the Nvidia boss was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy.

World.title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy
World.content:
Hundreds of billions of dollars have been wiped off the value of Nvidia after the US chipmaker announced an independent investigation would be carried out into its chief executive's affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

The tech firm saw its shares fall by about 4% by close of trade on Monday after Jensen Huang admitted having an extramarital affair.

Nvidia's probe came after reports that the US believed the Nvidia boss had been targeted in an espionage campaign by China.

However, China has rejected the claims, with its foreign ministry saying allegations about Chinese spies were "entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China".

Nvidia said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised, but a statement by the firm's board of directors said it would begin an investigation in "light of recent reporting that founder and chief executive Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort".

US intelligence officials believe Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was a spy for Beijing, according to a New York Times report, external.

The report said Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to top officials in Washington last spring warning that the Nvidia boss was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy.

Alice Huang was managing director of Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has had dealings with Nvidia.

Jensen Huang admitted he was "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children. He added he was "committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security" and would cooperate with the investigation.

The Nvidia co-founder has also been requested to appear for a joint closed-door briefing for several Congressional committees next week.

Members of the US House Foreign Affairs Committee last week asked Jensen Huang to appear for a closed-door briefing on his interactions with Alice Huang, as well as Nvidia's security protocols around espionage.

"Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC's [China's] access to sensitive US technology and information," congressmen Brian Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford wrote in a letter.

"It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which US national security has been placed at risk."

After Nvidia's investigation was announced, other big tech bosses, including Elon Musk, came out in support of Jensen Huang to continue leading the firm.

US President Donald Trump said the Nvidia boss was an "honourable guy".

However, the news sparked a sell-off in Nvidia's shares, with about $250bn (Â£190bn) wiped of the company's market value.

World.title: Ukraine peace talks resume with 'some flexibility' by warring sides, US officials say
World.content:
Moscow and Kyiv are privately showing "a little bit of flexibility" on the issue of who would controls Ukraine's eastern regions in a postwar scenario, US officials have said.

The comments came on the eve of the first trilateral talks aimed at ending the war in Ukraine since February.

Senior officials from Moscow, Kyiv and Washington will meet in Abu Dhabi as the fifth anniversary of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine approaches.

Jared Kushner - Donald Trump's son-in-law and part of the US delegation alongside peace envoy Steve Witkoff - said the talks would be focused on addressing the "postwar security concerns" of both Russia and Ukraine.

"An important part of this process is encouraging all parties to begin thinking seriously about what comes after the war," Kushner wrote on X.

But Moscow and Kyiv's positions on ending the conflict in the first place remain far apart.

A key area of disagreement between the two involves Ukraine's eastern region of Donetsk, which is by now mostly occupied by Russia.

Moscow has demanded that Ukraine relinquish the parts of Donetsk which it still holds, while Kyiv wants to freeze the contact line to maintain control over those sections, which it says are crucial to its future security.

While neither side has budged on these demands, the US official speaking on the eve of the talks suggested that this was just the public stance and that Moscow and Kyiv had shown "a little bit of flexibility, privately".

However, he acknowledged that the issue would not be solved without discussions about a new "security architecture".

"They will not solve the Donetsk issue and the territorial issue until they know what the security architecture is going to be after the war," the official said. "And keep in mind, we're not going to be able to finalise one without the other."

For Ukraine, a post-war "security architecture" may include reassurance that allies will come to its aid if it's attacked again. For Russia, that could be its longstanding ambition to see Nato roll back from eastern Europe â which would be alarming to Europeans.

The framework being proposed includes security consultations and crisis communications hotlines, as well as "reciprocal de-escalation measures" between the two. The officials also floated the re-activation of the Nato-Russia Council that has been largely paused since 2022.

World.title: Epstein associate who still runs model agency 'put me in danger' says abuse survivor
World.content:
If you are outside the UK, please watch on YouTube, external

An email in the DOJ files, from Fuller to Epstein, makes clear the close ties between the agency and the financier.

"Had it not been for you, we would have fired her months ago," Fuller writes of another model in March 2012. "And I would be careful as she blabs about things," he says.

A month after Epstein's second arrest in 2019, MC2's US branch was dissolved and Fuller opened a new agency, The Source Models, which is still operating. The BBC has found that 50 models from MC2 were transferred to his new agency.

We asked The Source Models to comment on our findings - it did not reply.

Model agencies were useful to Epstein, says Sigrid McCawley, the lead lawyer for more than 100 of Epstein's victims.

"Epstein said to many people he wanted three different girls a day. Think about those numbers... The [model] scouts were really critical because they were the ones who were identifying the type of woman that Epstein liked."

In the case of former agent Ramsey Elkholy, BBC Eye has discovered he tried to connect 34 women to Epstein, including an 18-year-old who was still in school.

The experience of one of the women highlights how assistants would be co-opted into the structure of the abuse.

Elkholy, the DOJ files show, suggested to Epstein that one of the financier's female assistants befriend this woman, before introducing her to Epstein.

We spoke to this woman, and she revealed that at her first meeting with Epstein, aged 19, he sexually abused her in his New York townhouse.

Ramsey Elkholy told the BBC: "I completely reject any allegation that I knew of or facilitated abuse of any kindâ¦ At the time, I had no knowledge of any abuse and I knew only his own [Epstein's] account of his 2008 [legal] case, which I misguidedly believed."

He continued: "The record and published reporting show that women were often groomed by other women in his inner circle. I was never part of that circle, or indeed of any such activityâ¦ my intention was to help models find professional opportunities by introducing them to an extremely well-connected individual."

If you are in the UK and you have been affected by any of the issues in this story such as sexual abuse and violence, information and support is available at BBC Action Line

Lawyer Sigrid McCawley says these female assistants would have had "no choice" in how they conducted themselves.

"These young survivors were being abused regularly. Their livelihoods were being threatenedâ¦ They had to do what they were being told to do."

Another model we have spoken to, Simona (not her real name), from eastern Europe, told us Epstein had raped her more than 200 times.

"People think that we gained something, that we agreed on this abuse in order to gain something, whether it's monetary or influential, but it's not true. We're left with deep trauma," says Simona.

She says the first time she met the financier, aged 20, she was already signed with a model agency in New York, and he offered to introduce her to his "good" friend Faith Kates.

At the time, Kates was the head of Next Management, one of the world's biggest model agencies. She stepped down from that senior executive position in December last year, but is still legally listed as a director of the company.

World.title: France accuses Iran of supermarket fridge hacking
World.content:
France has accused Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of being behind cyber-attacks that raised the temperatures of supermarket fridges and freezers across the country last month.

Foreign Minister Jean-NoÃ«l Barrot said the attack was "unprecedented in both its scale and its level of aggression", adding those who were responsible would be hit with sanctions.

Iran has yet to respond officially, but some Iranian media outlets have dismissed the allegations as baseless.

The French hacking, which led to the destruction of tons of frozen and chilled food in France was followed by a similar attack against supermarkets across several other European countries. It is not known if the instances are linked.

Barrot said the attack on France's supermarkets "marks the first large-scale cyber-attack aimed at sabotage on our national territory, and it constitutes a major attack on the nation's interests and the security of the French people".

He said the government had summoned the Iranian ambassador to Paris to "lodge a very strong protest against this extremely grave act".

France will take "any other necessary and proportionate measures" to respond to the incident and "deter anyone who might seek to repeat it", Barrot added.

The Paris prosecutor said an investigation had been opened into the head of an offensive cyber unit associated with the IRGC as well as his two deputies.

Laure Beccuau named the unit as Shahid Kaveh, which she said had an affiliation with the electronic and cyber centre of the IRGC.

Shahid Kaveh is the name given to a cluster of hackers thought to be directly employed by the Iranian regime.

In recent weeks, a number of commentators and politicians in Iran have argued that the country should extend any retaliation beyond the Middle East if the US and Israel resume the war they started earlier this year.

If the IRGC carried out the cyber-attacks, it remains unclear whether they were part of Iran's deterrence strategy.

On 11 October, hackers gained control of the software that regulates the temperatures of the refrigeration units used in many of France's supermarkets.

More than 100 of CoopÃ©rative U's supermarkets were hit, as well as 180 stores from IntermarchÃ© and its Netto brand. In some stores, temperatures of the fridges reportedly rose to 50C (120F) overnight.

Other major food retailers including Carrefour, Monoprix and E.Leclerc were also hit by the attack, which targeted software provided by Danish engineering firm Danfoss.

The software allows retailers to manage their cold units remotely.

Earlier this month a second wave of hacks took place, hitting more than 100 stores across Europe.

Supermarkets in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected, while a smaller number of shops were hit in countries including Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland.

Separately in August a small number of US military bases had fridges mysteriously malfunction, spoiling food. This incident is also being investigated as deliberate cyber-attacks, Reuters news agency has reported, citing sources familiar with the matter.

Since the waves of attacks on freezers, experts have been speculating which hacking groups could be responsible, with Iran being on a list of potential suspects.

In spite of a pair of Russian-aligned hacktivist groups claiming they were responsible on Wednesday, few believed them.

The French government has not said how it reached the conclusion that Iran was responsible, and attribution of cyber-attacks is extremely hard as hackers are able to hide their locations.

Additional reporting by Farshad Bayan, BBC Persian.

World.title: Republican congressman to force impeachment vote on Defence Secretary Hegseth
World.content:
A Republican congressman plans to force a vote in the House of Representatives this week to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, alleging he has violated the US Constitution.

"By engaging in hostilities in Iran for more than 90 days without congressional authorisation, Secretary Hegseth is breaking the law and must be held accountable," Representative Thomas Massie said.

The effort will likely fail, as Republicans remain in power in Congress until January. But Massie says the effort is aimed at pushing President Donald Trump to replace Hegseth before Democrats can launch their own impeachment process.

Hegseth has called the impeachment effort a "sham" and defended his record.

"You see, they attack me. They attack us because we are effective," he said in a video statement last week. "It's not going to work. We will not back down."

He called Massie a "disgruntled, defeated congressman" and said he was not concerned about the impeachment effort. In the video, Hegseth defended his leadership of the department and listed ways he has fulfilled Trump's America First agenda.

Massie formally introduced his articles of impeachment in a resolution on the House floor on Monday afternoon. The move starts a 48-hour clock for the chamber to take up the measure. Lawmakers could vote on the resolution directly, vote to refer it to committee or to set it aside.

"I'm doing this because it's the right thing to do," he told reporters after introducing the articles.

Massie, who lost re-election earlier this year, has been critical of Trump and the war in Iran since it started nearly nine months ago. He has previously garnered headlines over demanding the Trump administration release the files related to deceased sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

The Kentucky congressman first introduced impeachment articles in September and has now brought them back in the wake of Republicans losing control of both the House and Senate in last week's midterm elections.

He has said the effort was aimed at preventing a Democrat spectacle next year when they have control of Congress. He said he hoped to force Trump to name a replacement, who could be quickly confirmed while Republicans have power.

"My effort to impeach Secretary Hegseth is a much gentler version of what's coming when the Democrats assume control of the House and Senate next year," Massie also said in a statement. "They will hold hearings and trials."

Democratic leadership has signalled openness to such an effort against Hegseth once they take control in January.

Asked about the effort on Monday, Hegseth said, "We're not worried about that".

He said he planned to hold a news conference on Tuesday to discuss the subject.

President Trump has indicated that he plans to stick by Hegseth, praising his leadership in the US capture of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro earlier this year and defending his work during the war in Iran.

"We've made the world a lot safer place. Why haven't we gone after all these other people that ran wars and lost?" Trump said on Monday at the White House.

He also touted recruitment numbers under Hegseth.

"The soldiers, the actual soldiers, the great people that do the work, the great patriots, they love Pete Hegseth," he said. "He's done a very good job."

Impeaching a cabinet secretary is rare. It must be approved by both chambers for the secretary to be removed from office.

Trump was impeached by the House twice in his first term in office but was cleared by the Senate after two trials and not removed.

As with the presidential process, the House would first hold a vote on charges against Hegseth and the Senate then would conduct a trial to decide whether to acquit or convict.

The House has voted to impeach only two cabinet members in US history, but the Senate did not convict either one.

While impeachment has been "an incredibly rare process", it has become far more normalised since the House impeached President Bill Clinton in 1998, said Paul Gowder, a law professor at Northwestern University in Chicago.

He said it has become "much more common as the country has become more politically polarised," adding a prediction that several more of Trump's cabinet members may face impeachment over the next two years.

Massie told reporters he was not sure if the measure had sufficient backing to pass. It would need a majority to pass the House and even with all Democratic support, it would still likely need some Republican support as the party holds a slim majority.

Peter Loge, a professor of public affairs at George Washington University, told the BBC that he believed it was likely to pass due to those slim margins.

"There are enough angry Republicans that more than enough Republicans are gonna simply not show up to vote," he said.

Currently, there are 218 Republicans and 214 Democrats in the House.

While the House requires a simple majority to pass articles of impeachment, the Senate mandates a two-thirds vote to convict, threshold that is difficult to meet in the current congressional term.

When Democrats take over in January, they are likely to have at least 54 Senate seats - though two races do not yet have winners due to slim voting margins. A total of 60 votes will be required to convict and remove an official from office.

World.title: Qantas to outsource 850 local jobs with most roles moving to India
World.content:
Qantas will outsource 850 local corporate jobs to consulting giant Accenture with most roles moving to India as the airline fast-tracks AI investment.

In an internal email to staff on Tuesday, the Australian company's CEO Vanessa Hudson said "this is hard news for some and I'm sorry for the uncertainty it brings".

The job cuts will begin mid-2027, she said, and start with finance, procurement, people and marketing roles shifting "mostly" to teams in India and "some in Australia" as the firm seeks to modernise its IT systems.

Hudson said the "scale and speed of change in technology and AI is something none of us has seen in our lifetime", and it was in talks with unions and staff on the plans.

The move comes days after the airline provided a market update, flagging fare increases and flight cuts amid higher fuel costs.

On its new multi-year deal with Accenture, Hudson said it was about "modernising" the airline's IT systems to become "more efficient".

Qantas spends more than AU$1bn (US$691m; Â£514m) a year on technology, she said, and the company's back-end systems needed to be upgraded.

"Like every airline, we run on technology built up over decades for a different era, including more than 1,000 legacy applications that were never designed to work together," she said.

The deal with Accenture means "we will redesign and simplify parts of how our corporate functions work and reduce duplication", Hudson said, so staff can "spend more time on work that creates value for our customers and the business".

The company said that "in time", the work that Accenture takes over will be "transformed further with automation and AI".

Staff affected by the job cuts will be redeployed "where possible", the firm added, including new roles in Australia.

Qantas - which employs about 28,000 staff in Australia and another 4,000 globally - said thousands of its staff already use AI in their daily work.

The BBC has contacted the Australian Services Union for comment.

World.title: Russia's leading independent newspaper closes after eviction
World.content:
Russia's leading independent newspaper has closed after being evicted from its offices and facing pressure from authorities.

For 30 years, Novaya Gazeta published investigations into corruption, human rights violations and abuse of power in the country.

On Monday, the team behind the newspaper had a final editorial meeting before packing up their belongings and leaving.

The Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Russia's media was highly diverse and that the newspaper's closure was part of "a standard rotational process".

The BBC spoke to its co-founder Dmitry Muratov, a Nobel Peace Prize winner, about the closure.

More on this story.

World.title: Navy rescues Bayelsa commissioner, NSCDC official, 5 others from drowning
World.content:
The Nigerian Navy, in collaboration with members of the Abedigbene fishing community in Bayelsa State, have rescued seven boat passengers from drowning following a mishap in the area on Thursday.

The rescued passengers include the Bayelsa Commissioner for Trade, Industry and Investment, Ebieri Jones, a Nigerian Security and Civil Defence Corps official, and five other passengers.

This is contained in an operational report by the Director of Naval Information, Abiodun Folorunsho, made available to the News Agency of Nigeria on Saturday in Abuja.

Mr Folorunsho, a Navy captain, said the rescue was conducted by personnel of Forward Operating Base (FOB) FORMOSO in collaboration with local divers around the Abedigbene waters in Brass Local Government Area of the state.

“The incident involved a passenger boat travelling from Yenagoa to Akassa, which reportedly had eight persons on board.

“Following a distress report from a local fisherman, personnel deployed at Labrador Lagosgbene Houseboat promptly mobilised to the scene and commenced search and rescue operations.

“With the support of the community members, the survivors were found and taken to the houseboat, where they received first aid; preliminary assessments indicated no visible injuries,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The naval spokesperson added that one passenger, identified as a police officer, remained missing and assured that search and rescue efforts continued to locate the officer.

He explained that on Friday, the commissioner and the six other survivors were conveyed to Yenagoa to reunite with their respective families.

According to Mr Folorunsho, the operation highlights the Navy’s commitment to maritime safety, protecting lives, and responding promptly to emergencies within its area of responsibility.

He quoted the Commanding Officer, FOB FORMOSO, Sunday Haruna, as commending the personnel for their prompt response and professionalism, while acknowledging the invaluable support of the local divers and host community.

“The successful rescue further underscores the importance of collaboration between security agencies and coastal communities in strengthening maritime safety and protecting lives,” Mr Haruna, a captain, said.

World.title: Tinubu acknowledges challenges facing Nigerian youths, promises more opportunities
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has acknowledged growing concerns among Nigerian youths over unemployment, the rising cost of living, access to education and insecurity, saying his administration has a responsibility to address their expectations.

PREMIUM TIMES reports that Nigeria’s economic difficulties have been compounded by the shocks from the removal of petrol subsidies and the floating of the naira, with geopolitical conflicts and wars further disrupting global energy and commodity markets, worsening the cost-of-living pressures on households.

Persistent insecurity across several parts of the country has also crippled local economies, disrupted farming and commercial activities, displaced communities and forced the closure of schools, leaving millions of children exposed to prolonged educational disruption.

Mr Tinubu said young Nigerians deserved more than explanations about the economic difficulties facing the country, adding that his government was working to expand opportunities through investments in education, skills development, innovation and entrepreneurship.

The president spoke on Monday in Abuja at the closing ceremony of the 2026 National Youth Conference. His address was delivered by the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas.

“I understand the challenges confronting our young people. I know that many of you are concerned about employment, the cost of living, access to education, opportunities to start businesses and the security of your communities,” he said.

He also acknowledged young people’s desire for a country where hard work is rewarded, talent is recognised and opportunities are not determined by personal connections or one’s background.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“These are legitimate expectations. They are expectations that government has a responsibility to address,” he said.

Mr Tinubu said his administration’s Renewed Hope Agenda was designed to build an economy that creates opportunities, rewards enterprise and gives Nigerians a fair chance to succeed.

He acknowledged that the government’s economic reforms had come with sacrifices but said young people deserved to see the promised opportunities translate into tangible improvements in their lives.

“I know that these reforms have come with sacrifices. But I also know that young Nigerians deserve more than explanations about the difficulties of today.

“You deserve to see the opportunities of tomorrow becoming realities in your lives,” he said.

Mr Tinubu listed the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), the Three Million Technical Talent (3MTT) programme, YouthCred and the Nigerian Youth Academy among the initiatives his administration was implementing to expand opportunities for young people.

He said the government would do more to ensure that skills training leads to employment, innovation attracts investment, and young entrepreneurs have continued access to financing.

He also promised to support young Nigerians to succeed regardless of their backgrounds or locations.

World.title: INEC yet to receive court order on ADC, Tinubu, says Amupitan
World.content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says it has yet to receive Certified True Copies (CTCs) of recent Federal High Court rulings concerning African Democratic Congress (ADC) and the submission of President Bola Tinubu’s academic credentials.

INEC ​‌‌‍​‌‍⁠⁠‍‍​‍​⁠‌‌⁠‌​Chairman, Joash Amupitan, disclosed this while speaking at a news conference on the voter register on Monday in Abuja.

Responding to inquiries on the court order invalidating the candidacy of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and the David Mark-led ADC leadership last week, Mr Amupitan said that the commission “does not act on social media reports” but strictly on verified legal documents.

“As of today, I have not received a Certified True Copy of the judgement of the Federal High Court because we don’t just act on the basis of what is on social media.

“I remember one of the judgements of the Supreme Court sometime ago where something was posted on social media, trended, and the Supreme Court disowned itself from it, leading to investigations.

“Normally, when we receive a judgment like that, it comes to the commission, first to the chairman, who asks for expert advice from the relevant department before it is taken to the commission for review,” Mr Amupitan said.

On the court ruling ordering him to present Mr Tinubu’s credentials, Mr Amupitan maintained that he would only take necessary legal steps once formally served with the court order.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“I have not received the order. So, when I receive the order, I will look at what the order says and then know what to do accordingly,” he stated.

Addressing the requests for early voting provisions for journalists, security agencies and INEC officials on essential duties, the chairman noted that the proposal remained constrained by existing statutory frameworks.

“INEC initiated the process for early voting as part of the amendment of the Electoral Act, but it did not find support from the National Assembly to make provisions relating to early voting.

“So, this is still not known to our law, but it’s going to still be a process of advocacy to ensure that this is done,” he said.

Mr Amupitan confirmed that the 54 registration officers recently indicted for sabotaging voter registration procedures were full-time staff of the commission, asserting that INEC would not cover up any wrongdoing.

“Yes, I have the list here. They are all staff of INEC, and we are taking steps. We are not covering anything; what I told you today is just the truth,” he added.

Clarifying concerns about AI-generated images detected on the voter register, Mr Amupitan announced immediate technological upgrades to block future vulnerability exploits.

“We have just directed the Director of ICT that our web camera should not be allowed again. Instead, we should have an app camera. It is what is on the app that will take pictures; don’t go and use any URL to begin importing pictures here and there.

“Just today, the commission also approved the Artificial Intelligence (AI) Governance Framework to improve on what we used to have, developed in collaboration with IFES and the UK High Commission,” he said.

He warned that individuals involved in deliberate double registration or digital infractions would face criminal prosecution alongside security agencies’ ongoing investigations.

“For those of our staff and members of the public deliberately involved in acts of crime, where there is a commission of a crime, persons involved will be reported to the appropriate law enforcement agencies for necessary prosecution,” Mr Amupitan said.

(NAN)

World.title: Tinubu driving economic, security transformation in South-east – Shettima
World.content:
Vice-President Kashim Shettima says President Bola Tinubu’s administration is driving significant economic and security transformation across Nigeria’s south-east.

Mr Shettima stated this on Monday at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Abakaliki, Ebonyi State.

He said the Federal Government was investing in transportation, renewable energy, agriculture, housing and human capital development to unlock the region’s economic potential.

According to him, the interventions are designed to improve regional connectivity, strengthen food security, expand economic opportunities and address longstanding development challenges.

Mr Shettima cited major infrastructure projects, federal appointments and welfare programmes as evidence of Mr Tinubu’s commitment to Ebonyi and the wider South-east.

He identified the Calabar-Ebonyi-Benue-Kogi-Nasarawa-Abuja Superhighway as a major project expected to strengthen trade and economic integration across regions.

Other projects include the Ndibe Bridge, which will connect Ebonyi with Cross River State, and the ongoing Enugu-Abakaliki-Ogoja Expressway.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He also mentioned the Okposi-Ohaozara-Ukawu-Cross River Road, saying the projects would ease transportation and facilitate the movement of agricultural produce and manufactured goods.

The vice-president said improved road connectivity would reduce logistical challenges, enhance access to markets and increase business opportunities across the region.

On agriculture, Mr Shettima described Ebonyi as a major contributor to Nigeria’s food security, particularly through rice and cassava production.

He said the Federal Government was supporting farmers through fertiliser distribution, interest-free FarmerMoni assistance and other agricultural development programmes.

He added that rural road investments would enable farmers to access markets more easily, minimise post-harvest losses and improve their earnings.

Mr Shettima disclosed that thousands of Ebonyi residents had benefited from grants under the Presidential Conditional Grant Scheme and other federal employment and digital skills initiatives.

On security, he said the Tinubu administration had intensified efforts to restore stability across the South-east, stressing that economic development depended on safe communities and businesses.

He identified the Nigerian Army Recruits Training Depot at Amasiri-Edda, Ebonyi, as one of the Federal Government’s interventions to strengthen security in the region.

The vice-president also highlighted the establishment of the South-East Development Commission, the inauguration of South-East Vision 2050 and approval of the South-East Investment Company.

He said the initiatives were designed to accelerate regional development, attract investments and create sustainable economic opportunities.

Mr Shettima urged Ebonyi residents to renew their support for Mr Tinubu and the APC in the 2027 general elections, describing public office as a responsibility that must translate into tangible benefits.

He commended Governor Francis Nwifuru for directing increased state resources towards development projects and praised his administration’s efforts at responsible governance.

Umahi speaks on roads, other federal projects in South-east

Earlier, Minister of Works, Dave Umahi, attributed the massive turnout at the rally to Ebonyi’s support for the APC and Mr Tinubu.

Mr Umahi thanked the president for federal investments in road infrastructure across the state, involving hundreds of kilometres of highways and billions of naira in funding.

READ ALSO: Tinubu’s fresh Ibom Deep Seaport approval raises questions over Buhari’s 2020 clearance, financing

Earlier, the vice-president visited Fidelis Nwonumara, Eze Nnodo II of Amagu Autonomous Community and Chairman of the Izzi/Nnodo Traditional Rulers Council, where he received the chieftaincy title, Aka Ekpuchi Ọnwa.

The title, meaning “A Hand Cannot Cover the Moon”, symbolises truth, integrity and distinguished service, while reflecting the enduring friendship between Northern Nigeria and the South-east.

Mr Shettima described the honour as a responsibility to strengthen his relationship with Ebonyi and promote national unity, recalling the historic bonds of trade and friendship between both regions.

(NAN)

World.title: INEC removes 1.6 million names from voters’ register, fingers 54 officials
World.content:
Nigeria’s electoral commission, INEC, said it has identified 54 persons across 10 states who allegedly manipulated the voter registration procedures and contributed to irregularities in the preliminary register of voters, including AI-generated profiles.

Speaking at a press conference in Abuja on Monday, INEC Chairman, Joash Amupitan, said a technical assessment of the voters register revealed instances in which some registration personnel deliberately circumvented established procedures and abused provisions designed for exceptional registration circumstances, including those for persons with disabilities.

Mr Amupitan, a professor, said the affected records had been identified, reviewed, and corrected, while the personnel involved had been identified for further administrative investigation.

“Fifty-four persons cutting across 10 states have been identified as complicit, and necessary disciplinary action will be taken against them, including possible prosecution,” the INEC chairman said.

“To prevent recurrence, the commission is strengthening its registration controls with enhanced biometric capture, authentication and verification safeguards.”

He said the commission’s technical assessment examined suspected multiple registrations, unusual registration patterns, substituted photographs and irregularities associated with registration transactions.

Mr Amupitan said the commission was also examining historical irregularities in the register dating back to 2011, noting that some duplicated names and photographs circulated on social media were linked to earlier registration exercises.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said the commission would continue to investigate the circumstances surrounding the irregularities and strengthen its procedures to protect the integrity of the national register.

Concerns over AI, irregular profiles

INEC said the investigation followed public complaints about irregularities in the preliminary register of voters displayed at registration areas between 9 and 15 October 2026 and subsequently published online.

Nigerians raised concerns over the inclusion of suspicious profiles, including those suspected to be AI-generated, in the voters register published online on 26 October.

The complaints included allegations of multiple registrations, unusual names, artificial or manipulated photographs and deceased persons remaining on the register.

INEC removes 1.6 million records

According to the chairman, the commission has removed 1,608,660 confirmed invalid registrations from the preliminary register generated from the 2025/2026 Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) exercise.

Mr Amupitan said the commission, at its meeting on Monday, 9 November, directed that records already flagged through public complaints, as well as obvious cases, should be removed after proper verification.

INEC said its Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) initially flagged 1,545,052 of the 11,088,238 records harvested from the three phases of the 2025/2026 Continuous Voter Registration exercise for further examination.

Following additional public complaints, the commission reviewed 268,000 cases, of which 217,722 were invalidated while 50,278 were cleared and retained, the INEC chairperson said.

The INEC chairman explained that many of the multiple registrations and suspicious photographs circulating on social media related to records captured between 2011 and 2023, rather than the latest CVR exercise.

According to him, the national register has evolved through successive registration and continuous voter registration exercises since 2011, using different technologies, operational arrangements and quality standards.

World.title: Enugu governor appoints another Nollywood star as gubernatorial aide
World.content:
Governor Peter Mbah of Enugu State has appointed another popular Nollywood actress, Destiny Etiko, as a gubernatorial aide.

Ms Etiko is now a senior special assistant on Youth Engagement and Creative Economy to Mr Mbah.

Ms Etiko announced the appointment in a post on her Facebook page on Monday.

The Nollywood star thanked Mr Mbah for the confidence and opportunity he had given her to serve the state.

“I pledge my unwavering loyalty, dedication, and commitment to your administration’s vision and the good people of Enugu State.

“I embrace this responsibility with pride, humility and a determination to make a meaningful impact,” she stated.

It was unclear whether Ms Etiko had been appointed recently or was among the 101 new aides appointed to various positions in the state in September, including special adviser, senior special assistant and special assistant roles.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The 37-year-old has become the third Nollywood star to be appointed as Mr Mbah’s aide in recent times.

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the governor, in September, appointed popular Nollywood actress and filmmaker Eucharia Aṅunobi as his senior special assistant on women mobilisation for the Enugu North District.

Another Nollywood actress, Rachael Okonkwo, was also appointed by the governor as his senior special assistant on Film and Creative Industry Development.

Glance at Eucharia Aṅunobi

Born in Udi Local Government Area of Enugu State, Ms Etiko rose to prominence following her performance in the film called Idemili.

In 2021, the actress was honoured with the Nollywood Personality of the Year award at The Sun Awards for contributions to the Nigerian film industry.

Nollywood stars and creatives usually prefer to relocate to Lagos State for greater career opportunities, but Ms Etiko has remained in her home state of Enugu, where she was born.

With this appointment, she joins the list of Nollywood stars who have been given political appointments in Nigeria in the past.

READ ALSO: Enugu governor appoints two Nollywood stars as special assistants

Nkiru Sylvanus, another Nollywood actress, was appointed special assistant on Lagos State Affairs to the then Imo State Governor Rochas Okorocha in July 2011.

In April 2022, Governor Charles Soludo of Anambra State appointed Nollywood actor Bob-Manuel Udokwu as his special adviser on Entertainment, Leisure and Tourism.

World.title: Stallion Group partners with Access Bank
World.content:
Stallion Group has partnered with Access Bank, part of Access Holdings, Nigeria’s largest banking group by total assets, to make vehicle ownership more accessible. The partnership brings 10 exclusive automotive brands and 72 models within reach of customers.

Through Access Bank’s AutoFest initiative, eligible buyers can access financing of up to 90% of their chosen vehicle’s value, with a minimum 10% Equity contribution for individual and20%-30% for Fleet Financing. Delivery may be possible within 72 hours after Equity Contribution, subject to credit approval and completion of documentation.

With more than 50 years in the automotive industry, Stallion Group brings an established portfolio of international brands, exclusive manufacturer relationships and extensive customer support capabilities to the partnership.

The offering extends beyond vehicle sales. Customers can access professional servicing, Optimised Cost of ownership, genuine spare parts, dedicated bodyshop facilities, manufacturer warranties of up to six years on eligible vehicles, and electric vehicle battery warranties of up to eight years, subject to manufacturer terms and conditions.

Flexible repayment options extending beyond four years given individuals and businesses the opportunity to acquire vehicles without paying the full purchase price upfront.

The partnership combines Stallion Group’s automotive heritage and after sales infrastructure with the financial strength and reach of one of Africa’s largest banking groups.

10 Brands. 72 Models. Up to 90% Financing. Potential Delivery in 72 Hours.

World.title: Gombe: PDP ex-chairman, ex-SSG, others join APC
World.content:
The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Gombe State has recorded another wave of defections, with some of its leaders, including the immediate past state chairman, Joel Jagafa, and former Secretary to the State Government (SSG), James Pisagih, joining the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).

The development followed a meeting between the defectors and Governor Muhammadu Yahaya, where they formally declared their decision to join the APC and pledged their support for the governor’s leadership.

Others who defected include former PDP State Secretary, Buba Shanu; former Principal Officer of the Gombe State House of Assembly, Sunday Danlele; retired director, Mr Williams; and several other political stakeholders.

The meeting, facilitated by Ali Isa, allowed the former PDP chieftains to formally identify with the APC and express their commitment to the party.

The defectors said their decision was driven by confidence in Governor Yahaya’s leadership, political direction and the performance of his administration.

They also pledged to contribute their political experience, grassroots connections, and networks to strengthen the APC’s structures and mobilise support for the party across the state.

Welcoming them, Governor Yahaya described their decision to join the APC as a positive development, noting that their arrival would expand the party’s membership and strengthen its political base in Gombe State.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He assured the new members of equal opportunities and inclusiveness, stressing that the APC remained open to individuals willing to work towards the party’s ideals and collective aspirations.

The governor expressed confidence that their experience and contributions would support the party’s activities and further consolidate its structures across the state.

World.title: Canada makes rural immigration programme permanent
World.content:
By Favour Ulebor

Canada has made its Rural Community Immigration Pilot a permanent programme to attract and retain skilled foreign workers in smaller communities facing persistent labour shortages.

The Minister of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship, Lena Metlege Diab, announced the decision on Monday, November 9, 2026, in Pictou County, Nova Scotia.

According to a statement published on the website of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC), the programme will initially retain the 14 communities currently participating in the pilot, with plans to expand to more communities in the future.

The employer- and community-driven programme is designed to address labour shortages in rural areas by connecting skilled foreign workers and their families with employers and community support services.

It also seeks to encourage newcomers to settle permanently in smaller communities and contribute to their economic development.

Speaking during the announcement, Diab said the government recognised the critical role rural communities played in Canada’s economy despite the challenges they faced in attracting workers.

“Our government understands that rural communities play a critical role in powering Canada’s economy. At the same time, many face real challenges finding the workers they need.

“That’s why we’re transitioning our successful rural immigration pilot into a permanent program—helping smaller communities attract and retain essential workers who deliver services and drive economic growth.

“We appreciate that a one-size-fits-all approach to immigration doesn’t work for rural Canada, and this permanent pathway is one part of our work to ensure that communities of all sizes can share in the benefits of responsible, sustainable immigration,” she said.

Under Canada’s 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan, the government has allocated 5,500 admission spaces to the permanent Rural Community Immigration Program.

The government said the initiative was part of its broader immigration policy aimed at stabilising the number of immigrants admitted into the country, reducing the temporary resident population and retaining skilled foreign workers already contributing to local communities.

It added that preliminary results from the pilot showed that foreign workers had helped address labour shortages in critical sectors, including healthcare, education, sales and services, between 2025 and 2026.

The department also disclosed that participating communities had vetted and designated more than 1,950 trusted employers experiencing persistent labour shortages that could not be addressed through the local workforce between January 2025 and August 2026.

The transition to a permanent programme is expected to provide rural employers with a more reliable supply of skilled foreign workers while supporting the long-term economic development of participating communities.

World.title: Trump says Nvidia boss Huang had ‘no idea’ lover was alleged Chinese spy
World.content:
WASHINGTON, DC – NOVEMBER 09: U.S. President Donald Trump speaks in the James S. Brady Press Briefing Room of the White House on November 09, 2026 in Washington, DC. Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images/AFP (Photo by CHIP SOMODEVILLA / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP)

US President Donald Trump said Monday that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had “no idea” that a woman he had affair with was an alleged Chinese spy, adding that Huang was “suffering greatly.”

“I asked him that question, ‘did you have any idea that she was a spy?’ He said ‘I had no idea that she was a spy,’ and I really believe him,” Trump told reporters at the White House.

World.title: I’m a godfather, but I don’t impose appointments on governors — Osoba
World.content:
Former Ogun State Governor, Olusegun Osoba

By Efe Onodjae

Former Ogun State Governor, Olusegun Osoba has defended the role of political godfathers in Nigeria’s democracy, saying their responsibility should be to offer advice and guidance rather than impose political appointees on elected governors.

Osoba, who spoke during a podcast hosted by Reuben Abati and shared on X (formerly Twitter), said he considered himself a political godfather but had deliberately avoided interfering in the administration of his political successors.

According to him, he had never nominated anyone for appointment as commissioner, special adviser, councillor or local government chairman in the state.

He said: “I agree, I’m a godfather. But one thing that is working for me in my state is that I hardly interfere. I counsel and advise him. I have never nominated one person into his government.”



Explaining his position, the former governor said imposing candidates on an administration could undermine the governor’s authority and create unnecessary divisions among his political supporters.

He noted that appointing one person from the numerous people around him could offend others, while anyone recommended by him might be viewed with suspicion within the administration.



Osoba recalled that during his tenure as governor, he adopted a system that allowed each federal constituency to nominate candidates for commissioner positions.

He said he requested one name from each federal constituency and subsequently reviewed their credentials before assigning them portfolios, adding that the approach helped him avoid pressure from political associates.

The former governor maintained that political godfathers should ensure that people who worked for a candidate during electioneering campaigns were recognised and compensated, but should not dictate how an elected governor runs his administration.

“That’s the role of a godfather. I agree, I’m a godfather,” he said.



Osoba also defended the participation of experienced elders in candidate selection, citing his support for a presidential candidate whom he described as experienced, having served in the Lagos State House of Assembly, House of Representatives and Senate, as well as in the corporate sector.

World.title: Charlie Kirk murder trial set for June 2028, suspect faces death penalty
World.content:
(Rick Egan | The Salt Lake Tribune) Tyler Robinson, accused in the fatal shooting of Charlie Kirk, appears during a hearing in 4th District Court in Provo, Thursday, Dec. 11, 2025.

The trial of the man accused of murdering US conservative firebrand Charlie Kirk will begin in June 2028, the judge said Monday.

“Jury selection will begin June 21, 2028,” judge Tony Graf told the Utah district court, noting that 105 days have been reserved for the trial.

Tyler Robinson, 23, faces a potential death penalty for allegedly killing Kirk with a gunshot to the neck on a university campus in the western US state of Utah on September 10, 2025.

The killing of Kirk at age 31 at an event planned by his right-wing youth organization, Turning Point, sent shockwaves through the US political world.

Kirk had become a popular leader in a Christian Nationalist movement that preaches traditional values while voicing intolerance for diversity and LGBTQ communities.

Turning Point was key to mobilizing youth support for Donald Trump’s re-election as president in 2024. The group is now led by his wife, Erika Kirk.

The prosecution had sought a trial as early as January 2028, while Robinson’s lawyers had wanted until the end of 2029 to prepare their defense.

Last month, Trump criticized the judge and said the case “should be tried within a month, not three years.”

Kirk’s assassination last year triggered a 33-hour manhunt culminating in Robinson surrendering to authorities.

He has pled not guilty.

The prosecution has presented text messages in which Robinson confessed to planning the murder to his roommate, a transgender person with whom they allege Robinson was in a relationship.

The defense has focused on alleged weaknesses in the DNA and ballistic evidence.

World.title: Governor Idris pardons, reinstate suspended Commissioner in Kebbi
World.content:
Gov Nasir Idris of Kebbi State.

By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi

Kebbi State Governor, Dr. Nasir Idris has directed the reinstatement of the Commissioner for Animal Health, Husbandry and Fisheries, Alhaji Kabir Usman Alaramma, to his position.

The Honourable Commissioner for Information and Culture, Alhaji Yakubu Ahmed Birnin Kebbi, disclosed this shortly after the State Executive Council meeting presided over by Governor Nasir Idris at the Council Chamber of Government House, Birnin Kebbi.

According to the Commissioner, the reinstatement of the suspended Commissioner is with immediate effect.

With this directive, the Commissioner of Information stated, the suspension previously imposed on the Commissioner had formally been lifted.

“Consequently, he has been reinstated to his position and is hereby directed to resume his official duties with immediate effect,” the Commissioner said.

The reinstatement underscores the commitment of the Kebbi State Government to effective governance, administrative responsibility, and the continued strengthening of party and stakeholder engagement across the state.

World.title: Full list: 2026/2027 FA Cup second round fixtures confirmed
World.content:
Wimborne Town have been handed a home tie against Bradford City in the second round of the FA Cup, while Leicester City will travel to non-league side Dover Athletic.

Seventh-tier Wimborne are among the lowest-ranked teams remaining in the competition after producing one of the biggest upsets of the first round by defeating League Two side Crawley Town.

The Magpies will now welcome League One outfit Bradford City as they look to continue their impressive FA Cup run.

Leicester, who won the competition in 2021, must overcome Dover Athletic away from home to book their place in the third round.

Leyton Orient will host Port Vale, last season’s quarter-finalists, while 2013 FA Cup winners Wigan Athletic have been drawn against Barnsley in an all-League One encounter.

Jack Wilshere’s Luton Town will travel to AFC Fylde, while the winner of the postponed Plymouth Parkway versus Berkhamsted tie will host Barnet.

The second-round fixtures will be played across the weekend of December 5, 2026.

World.title: Jensen Huang: 5 things to know about viral Nvidia CEO’s affair with Chinese executive
World.content:
(FILES) Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang speaks during Nvidia Live at CES 2026 ahead of the annual Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas, Nevada, on January 5, 2026. Chip giant Nvidia’s board announced on November 8, 2026 it opened a probe into Chief Executive and co-founder Jensen Huang after he acknowledged an affair with a woman US officials say was working for Chinese intelligence. (Photo by Patrick T. Fallon / AFP)

Nvidia chief Jensen Huang, whose chips power the global AI boom and who has the ear of President Donald Trump, has admitted to an affair with a Chinese executive who US intelligence reportedly believes was working for Beijing.

Here is what we know:

– What happened? –

Huang, 63, acknowledged the relationship Sunday in a message to Nvidia employees.

“I was unfaithful to my wife,” he wrote. “My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”

Huang has been married to his wife Lori since 1985.

His admission followed reports in The New York Times that US intelligence officials had concluded the woman, Alice Huang, was passing information to China. She is not related to the Nvidia chief.

Nvidia had previously said that his interactions with her were “not unusual or unexpected” given their business ties.

– Who is Alice Huang? –

Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was a senior executive at Megaspeed. The Singapore-based data center company was spun off from a Chinese company in 2023, and it rents out computing power from Nvidia chips.

The Wall Street Journal reported that she and Huang were photographed together in Taipei in 2024 and 2025.

According to the Times, a memo circulated among senior US officials this spring cited intelligence that she was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security.

The memo said she had been recruited to gather information on Huang and possibly to steer Nvidia toward pushing for its top chips to be sold in China.

The Journal said that authorities in Singapore and Taiwan also suspected Chinese intelligence had recruited her after learning of her closeness to Huang. Her current whereabouts are unclear.

US officials suspect Megaspeed of helping smuggle restricted chips into China and the Justice Department has taken over a federal investigation into the company.

Megaspeed has previously described itself as a “compliant and legitimate company.”

Beijing rejected the allegations. Foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said Monday that “the narrative of a so-called Chinese spy is entirely baseless vilification and smearing.”

– Why does it matter? –

Nvidia controls an estimated 90 percent of the market for the chips used to train and run AI models. Washington has restricted sales of the most advanced ones to China since 2022 under the Biden administration.

Huang has also been one of Trump’s most influential informal advisers on AI.

The Journal reported that intelligence officials suspected the affair while Huang was lobbying the White House to allow chip exports to China.

Late last year, he pushed to sell Nvidia’s most powerful chips there, an effort that Secretary of State Marco Rubio and other officials blocked.

Trump instead allowed sales of a less advanced chip, with the US government taking a 25 percent cut.

According to the Times, Trump was briefed on the intelligence roughly a year ago and did not act on it.

On Fox News on Sunday, Trump was asked whether Huang should remain CEO. “I think so, oh yeah, sure,” he said, calling Huang “an honorable guy.” Trump said he did not regret not acting on the intelligence.

– What is the board doing? –

Nvidia’s board on Sunday said it had opened an independent probe into the matter.

“While the board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the board’s inquiry will examine all available information,” it said.

According to the Times, a committee of independent directors working with outside counsel will lead the review, and Huang will remain CEO in the meantime.

– What comes next? –

Republican House committee leaders, including those on the Select Committee on China, have asked Huang to attend a closed-door briefing on Nvidia’s security protocols in Washington on November 18.

Analyst Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives predicted the episode would lead to multiple congressional inquiries. He said Huang would likely keep his job in the near term but could be ousted depending on the internal inquiry’s findings.

George Chen of The Asia Group told AFP it would be “premature to conclude that Jensen poses a threat to US national security before the facts are fully established.”
