World.title: US-mediated talks with Russia and Ukraine to start in Abu Dhabi
World.content:
ABU DHABI: Negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the United States will hold talks in Abu Dhabi Tuesday on ending Europe’s worst conflict since World War II in the first such meeting in more than nine months, as another winter of war approaches.

Europe — alarmed by US President Donald Trump floating a deal with Moscow on European security ahead of the talks — will also send representatives to Abu Dhabi.

Trump has pushed for an end to the Russia-Ukraine war since returning to power, but previous talks produced no breakthroughs and the process became sidelined by the US-Israeli war against Iran.

Europe and Ukraine fear the United States will force a deal on Kyiv that would amount to a de-facto capitulation, with Trump appearing to pivot toward Moscow this year.

Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine has killed hundreds of thousands, displaced millions and has dragged on for 56 months, with the Kremlin showing no sign of backing down.

Trump hinted Ukraine will have to give up land ahead of the talks, saying: “They’re going to end up with a little bit different shape, Ukraine.”

Russia occupies large swathes of Ukraine but, while its troops have grinded westwards, they have not been able to seize the whole of the Donetsk region.

Moscow demands Kyiv surrender the parts of the region it still controls, vowing it will otherwise press on with its offensive.

Ukraine — which for more than 4.5 years has resisted a far larger invading army at a huge human cost — has ruled out such a withdrawal.

Russia pummeled Ukraine in the run-up to the talks and carried out one of its deadliest strikes yet — with Kyiv saying 55 people were killed in a frontline village as they queued for humanitarian aid.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the intensified strikes were part of Moscow’s strategy of “putting pressure on Ukraine’s position” at the negotiations.

Russia’s Vladimir Putin, who launched the war in February 2022, has repeatedly refused broader ceasefire offers and face-to-face talks with Zelensky.

Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner and special envoy Steve Witkoff will gather the enemy sides in Abu Dhabi for the first time since February, when negotiations took place in Geneva.

Russia and Ukraine have held several rounds of failed talks during almost five years of war and hopes for peace are low.

“We don’t have any particular expectations,” a senior Ukrainian official in Kyiv told AFP.

‘We don’t want Yalta 2.0’

Trump last week floated a “very big agreement” on the war that will “involve all of Europe,” stoking fears Washington would collaborate with Moscow on creating a new European security architecture.

Shortly before launching its 2022 invasion, Moscow had issued an ultimatum to the West for NATO to rollback troops from Eastern Europe.

The diplomat who issued the demand, Sergei Ryabkov, will for the first time be part of Moscow’s delegation, which is headed by Putin’s nationalistic aide Vladimir Medinsky.

Kushner said Monday that a peace settlement will require direct Russia-Europe talks “on the broader security arrangements that affect them” and said the US “recognizes difficult decisions ahead.”

These announcements have stoked fears in European capitals.

“For Europe, it is clear: we do not need to establish a new security architecture for Europe,” German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said Monday.

He urged Moscow to “give up maximalist demands” and warned against any “negotiation show” in the UAE capital.

Zelensky has warned of a “Yalta 2.0” referring to Western leaders dividing Europe with the USSR in 1945.

According to Ukraine’s chief negotiator Rustem Umerov, representatives from the UK, France, Germany and Italy, as well as NATO and EU officials will hold separate talks with Kyiv’s representatives in Abu Dhabi.

The Kremlin — which has sought to keep Europe out of the talks — said negotiations will remain “trilateral.”

A recent ceasefire in the Kherson region was “a very positive precedent,” Ukrainian political expert Volodymyr Fesenko told AFP, predicting Kyiv will look for “de-escalation of the war through such local truces.”

Kushner and Witkoff have been accused by critics of being soft on Russia and US media have reported that the Americans are pushing large back-door business deals with Moscow.

World.title: Trump says Iran war is militarily ‘effectively over’ after Qatar PM talks
World.content:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said on Monday there was “positive momentum” toward a deal to end the Iran war after meeting Qatar’s prime minister at the White House.

He told reporters he believes the war in Iran “militarily is effectively over” and “we’re just keeping it the status quo.”

He added that Iran has been “decapitated” but said he is still looking to make sure there’s a long-term solution to ensuring that Iran’s nuclear program is defanged.

Trump added in a post on Truth Social that a resumption of US military strikes on Iran was “quite unlikely,” saying that Gulf powers wanted to keep the status quo.

“I had an excellent conversation with Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani,” Trump said on Truth Social, adding that “much was discussed with respect to the Islamic Republic of Iran.”

In his post on Monday, Trump reiterated that the US was “locked and loaded,” but that he believed further strikes were “quite unlikely” given that key US allies in the Gulf “would prefer the status quo.”

“We are seeing positive momentum toward an end to this Conflict, and will ensure that America’s interests are at all times protected,” Trump said.

Trump’s comments echoed early statements to CNN over the weekend when he said it was “highly unlikely” fighting would resume.

Qatar Prime Minister ​Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani said he ‌had ‌positive ​discussions ‌with US ⁠President ​Donald Trump ⁠and Vice President JD Vance ⁠on ‌Monday.

“We discussed the situation in the region and ways to progress the US-Iran talks. Grateful for ‌the ​positive ‌discussions ‌on reaching a deal and ‌bringing peace to the ⁠region,” he ⁠said on X.

World.title: Russia’s Lavrov says US diesel deal working, prices coming down
World.content:
Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov ‌said the accord under which Russia is to supply diesel to the US and world markets is already working and ​lowering prices, writing in a piece published on Tuesday in Moscow daily Kommersant.

Lavrov said Russia was distinct from the West in not using its economy to score political points against countries seen as adversaries or competitors.

“Since 2022, we have supplied Europe with energy resources worth $320 billion,” Lavrov wrote in Kommersant.

“An important contribution to ‌energy security was ‌the agreement between the Russian ​and ‌US ⁠leaders to ​suspend restrictions on ⁠the export of Russian diesel. We have already started implementing it, which immediately brought prices down.”

US President Donald Trump announced on October 9 the surprise deal under which Russia agreed to immediately export 300,000 metric tons, or 2.25 million barrels, to the US and global ⁠markets, followed by 500,000 tons in November ‌and 1 million tons “immediately thereafter” ‌to help lower fuel prices ahead ​of the US midterm ‌elections.

His administration temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel ‌that were designed to deprive Moscow of revenue for its war on Ukraine.

Lavrov, in his comments to Kommersant, said Russia was working to stabilize world energy markets “ensuring global energy security, balanced ‌and sustainable development of countries and macro-regions.”

He did not give any data on diesel ⁠prices. ⁠US futures prices have fallen about 11 percent since the deal was announced, but at the pump in the US, diesel prices were at a record high last week when Americans voted, according to price tracker GasBuddy.

Lavrov said Ukraine was ignoring Trump’s calls to stop strikes on Russian energy targets. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky last week said Kyiv’s forces were pursuing their strikes.

Russian media said fuel shortages had returned to at least half ​a dozen Russian regions ​after Ukrainian strikes on at least eight major oil refineries in the past two weeks.

World.title: Sabalenka, Andreeva make winning starts at WTA Finals
World.content:
INDIAN WELLS, CA: World number two Aryna ‌Sabalenka got her WTA Finals campaign off to a winning start with a hard-fought victory over Karolina Muchova, while Mirra Andreeva eased past Elina Svitolina as Group ​2 action got underway on Monday.

Making her sixth consecutive appearance at the season-ending tournament, Sabalenka had to work hard to overcome a determined Muchova 7-6(2) 7-5, with the Czech making her debut at the event after a breakthrough season that included titles in Doha and Bad Homburg and a run to the Wimbledon final.

The Belarusian, who is seeking her first WTA Finals crown, had to dig deep in ‌the opening ‌set, breaking back when Muchova served for it ​at ‌5-4 ⁠before ​dominating the ⁠ensuing tiebreak to take the lead after almost an hour.

Sabalenka appeared to have gained control in the second set with a 4-2 lead, but the Czech refused to go away, breaking back when her opponent was serving for the match to level at 5-5.

Muchova’s resistance proved short-lived, however, as Sabalenka broke again before finally serving out the contest.

“She’s such ⁠an incredible player. Always tough battles. I was just ‌trying to stay calm and focus point ‌by point. She can come back any ​time. You have to be ‌focused from beginning till the end,” Sabalenka said on court.

“I’m super ‌happy with the level I played. To get the first win, it’s really important. Great start.”

In a meeting between youth and experience, French Open champion Andreeva made an impressive debut by dispatching the 2018 WTA Finals champion Svitolina 6-4 ‌6-0.

The Russian needed just one break of serve to take the opening set before raising her level ⁠considerably in the ⁠second, where she swept through all six games to complete a commanding victory.

Svitolina, who beat Andreeva at the Australian Open, struggled to find answers this time around, failing to convert any of the six break points she earned.

“I was trying to think about was that she beat me in Australia earlier this year. I really tried not to think about the match we had last year on these courts,” Andreeva said of her 2025 Indian Wells win over Svitolina.

“I remember how I was playing when I beat her here, but I knew ​it would be a tricky ​match. She’s an amazing player. I’m just very happy I was able to get through the match.”

World.title: Iraq to reopen Sheeb border crossing with Iran, temporarily close Mandali border
World.content:
CAIRO: Iraq will reopen the Sheeb border crossing with Iran ​on Tuesday morning after completing technical requirements and necessary procedures, the head of the country’s Border Ports Authority said, according to state news agency INA.

The authority will temporarily close the Mandali ‌border crossing with ‌Iran from ​Friday ‌to ⁠complete technical requirements, ​INA ⁠reported.

The developments come after Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said that the US Treasury had asked Baghdad to close all border crossings with Iran except for ⁠two, as part of Washington’s ‌efforts to ‌increase economic pressure on ​Tehran.

“There are ‌many official and unofficial border ‌crossings with Iran, and closing all of them would be difficult and would affect our economy. The Americans ‌are still demanding the closure of the crossings, and we ⁠are ⁠currently in discussions with them,” Hussein told Al Jazeera.

Iraq closed last month the busy Sheeb border crossing with Iran to review security and install detection equipment to stop smuggling.

It was not immediately clear whether the planned reopening of Sheeb or the ​temporary closure ​of Mandali was related to the US request.

World.title: UFC chief declines Trump’s White House job offer
World.content:
WASHINGTON, United States: Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief Dana White turned down President Donald Trump’s — apparently jovial — offer of a job as press secretary in a surprise appearance at the White House on Monday.

Trump stunned the world by saying on social media on Saturday that he had asked White to take on the high-profile post — but a day later the 80-year-old president said he was “only kidding.”

The 57-year-old cage fighting boss visited the White House on Monday, and Trump brought him out for a chaotic news conference in the James Brady Briefing Room.

“So let me ask you the big question. Would you like to be press secretary of the United States of America? Or do you just want to stay with this ridiculous UFC? Huh?” Trump said.

“Thank you for the offer, sir — for the offer, I have no, no — I do not want to be in politics,” White replied.

Trump smiled and headed out of the room, saying: “I am devastated to hear this. Goodbye, everybody.”

The press secretary’s post has been vacant since Katie Zacharia left on October 16 after less than a week in the post. Her combative predecessor Karoline Leavitt left in August after a year and a half in the job.

Trump’s announcement that he had offered the high-profile job to “violent Fighter and Warrior” White had sparked speculation that he was ready for a aggressive stance after the Republican Party’s stunning midterm elections defeat.

White is a long-time friend of the president and helped host a massive UFC match on the White House lawn earlier this year.

But there was also some skepticism about the president’s announcement, and Trump said Sunday night that he had been joking.

‘Beat the hell out of you’

Leading out White to the podium on Monday, Trump said he had been “having a little fun.”

“He’s a great guy,” Trump told the room full of reporters. “The only problem is he’ll talk for a little while and then he’s going to beat the hell out of you.”

Standing at the lectern and wearing a black t-shirt and jacket, White looked like he might be more comfortable in the octagon — the ring used for UFC fights.

“I’ve always wanted to do this. Who has the first question?” he joked — before quickliy adding: “I have zero political aspirations.”

White added that “the last 24 hours of my life has been insane” since Trump made the announcement.

Asked by a journalist to confirm he had said no to the job, White added: “I don’t tell the president ‘no’ to anything... I didn’t want to be disrespectful and say anything until he said something first.”

Trump then took a series of questions on more weighty matters, from the Iran and Ukraine wars to the possible impeachment of Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth and a spy scandal engulfing Nvidia boss Jensen Huang.

World.title: Zelensky says Ukrainian battlefield successes strengthen Kyiv’s position in talks
World.content:
President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Monday, on the eve of US-led, three-sided talks on resolving the war with Russia, that Ukrainian battlefield ​successes and mounting Russian losses were strengthening Kyiv’s position in negotiations.

The talks with Russian and US negotiators, opening on Tuesday in Abu Dhabi, will be the first since February aimed at bringing closer an end to the more than 4-1/2-year-old war.

“Ukrainian forces are currently genuinely strengthening Ukraine’s negotiating position,” Zelensky said in his nightly video address.

“Every task that is fully accomplished, every defensive operation ‌that increases ‌Ukraine’s strength and delivers results, strengthens Ukraine ​and, ‌above ⁠all, ​strengthens us ⁠in negotiations.”

Zelensky said top Ukrainian military commander Mykhailo Drapatyi had presented a report on Ukrainian military positions underscoring heavy recent losses by Russian forces. And he said Ukraine’s long-range strikes on Russian targets, including oil industry sites, were also working.

“These days, our defenders, both men and women, are achieving record results in eliminating Russian occupiers. Russia ⁠is suffering record losses on the front, every ‌day and every week,” Zelensky said.

“We ‌are responding to Russia’s war in ​a fully justified manner and demonstrating ‌that this war must end. Russia can do this. It ‌can end its war. It is important that the United States convince Russia of precisely this.”

The 1,200-km (775-mile) front line in the war has remained fairly static for many months and Ukrainian officials say Russia’s slow, long-running ‌westward advance through the eastern Donetsk region has slowed further.

Zelensky last month pointed to successes in ⁠offensive operations in ⁠specific theaters.

Russian forces hold about 20 percent of Ukrainian territory and President Vladimir Putin says Moscow’s objective remains to bring all of the eastern Donbas region under its control.

Russian commanders say their forces are continuing to advance on all sectors of the front and dismiss any suggestion that Ukraine’s military is making headway in recapturing territory.

Earlier, Zelensky’s chief of staff, Kyrylo Budanov, said while on his way to Abu Dhabi that maintaining the diplomatic process was important at the talks and Kyiv would focus ​on prisoner exchanges and other ​humanitarian issues.

Ukraine’s delegation to the talks is being led by Rustem Umerov, the head of foreign intelligence.

World.title: Families in Gaza patch torn shelters as rain exposes the misery and dangers of life in flimsy tents
World.content:
LONDON: Jehad Al-Jarbou’s young son danced in the rain, but inside the family’s tent in Gaza City water soaked their clothes and blankets.

For the little boy, his mother said, the downpour was a discovery. For Al-Jarbou, a Palestinian visual artist and poet, it exposed how little stood between her family and the harsh effects of the approaching winter.

“My son began dancing in the rain but now he is ill because we do not have adequate heating or proper clothes,” she told Arab News.

“A little child feels joy when he looks up at the sky and sees the rain. But the rain has drenched everything: his clothes, his bedding and his dreams.”

Across Gaza, torrential rain in recent days has flooded displacement camps, ruined bedding and left families patching shelters with whatever salvaged wood and scraps of fabric they can get their hands on. Aid groups have warned that Israeli restrictions on shelter supplies and reconstruction materials have turned foreseeable winter storms into emergencies.

The potentially life-threatening danger was made clear on Sunday night when a sand embankment weakened by rain collapsed onto tents in a camp south of Deir Al-Balah, killing a woman and five children, according to media reports and aid organizations.

“The number of fatalities is expected to rise,” said Wassem Mushtaha, Oxfam’s response lead in Gaza, on Monday.

Describing the conditions as “abhorrent,” he said that “severe flooding has displaced around 100,000 people.”

He added: “Israel is restricting access to shelter materials and has rendered 65 percent of Gaza off-limits. People have no safe place to go.”

People search for survivors at the site of a deadly sand embankment collapse at a camp for displaced Palestinians in Deir Al-Balah, in the central Gaza Strip on November 9, 2026. (AFP)

Videos showed men searching beneath boulders, sand and collapsed tents by the light of their phones after the embankment collapsed. Rescue teams were still looking for two missing persons on Monday, Save the Children said, warning that further landslides and collapsing buildings could endanger more families.

The organization said the Israeli military control of approximately 70 percent of Gaza had forced much of the Palestinian population into areas ill-equipped to withstand heavy rainfall. The families in Deir Al-Balah had been sheltering in the shadow of the sandbank that gave way. For those whose tents remained standing, the immediate challenge was finding somewhere safe and dry to sleep and provide protection from the next storm.

Al-Jarbou said her family had been trying to buy tarpaulins to reinforce their tent, despite high prices of about $100 each. When the first heavy downpour of the season arrived, she sat with her mother, brother and son. The heavy rain persisted for hours, soaking their belongings and washing away the ground around them. Sewage mixed with the rainwater, leaving pools of contamination that were a particular danger to her son.

“It’s very difficult to keep a young child from touching the rain when he sees it for the first time,” she said. “The ground is filthy because sewage mixes with the rainwater. Everywhere, there are pools of contaminated water.

“Nothing can protect us except being in a proper home. We need mobile homes, not tents.”

About 70,000 tents providing shelter for an estimated 350,000 people, including 210,000 children, flooded during 12 hours of torrential rain over the past few days, according to Palestinian media.

Save the Children warned that wet shelters and soaked winter clothing were exposing children to the risks of hypothermia and waterborne diseases. More than 2,000 damaged or structurally unsound buildings were also said to be at risk of collapse amid continuing rain and strong winds.

A displaced Palestinian boy wades through a water puddle between flooded tents amid heavy rainfall in Gaza City's Al-Remal neighbourhood on November 7, 2026. (AFP)

Even before the storm, families had few resources left with which to protect themselves, said Elias, an educator from Gaza City whose name has been changed at his request.

He described a sudden shift from prolonged heat to fierce winds, heavy rain and bitter cold, which was “making living conditions and health problems far worse.”

He told Arab News: “Families in displacement camps could not sleep because of the heavy rain. Their tents were torn apart and thousands collapsed or flooded, along with the bedding laid on the ground.”

Tens of thousands of people were now trying to repair the damage to their only shelter with worn-out fabric, poor-quality timber and metal salvaged from bombed homes, he said.

“I wish I could advise my loved ones to start digging caves and sheltering in them, as people did in medieval and prehistoric times, to experience that way of life while the rest of the world lives in the age of space exploration and technology,” Elias said.

“I don’t even know if the pieces of cloth that are sheltering displaced families deserve to be called tents at all,” he added, because the use of the word obscured how little protection they offered and “serves as a label that absolves the world’s governments and international institutions of responsibility.”

Aid organizations said emergency repairs might ease the immediate suffering but could not replace safe housing and functioning infrastructure.

Teams from Oxfam were working to maintain drainage networks, supply sandbags and repair tools, clear sewer blockages and drain floodwater from displacement sites, Mushtaha said, but they urgently needed spare parts, engine oil, pipes, heavy machinery and more shelter materials.

“Israel’s ongoing genocide has resulted in the near collapse of all functioning systems in Gaza,” he said. He called on governments to “insist that Israel allows for unimpeded access to recovery and repair materials to restore essential infrastructure and ensure Palestinian-led reconstruction efforts across Gaza.”

A child (L) looks through the opening of a tent at the site of a deadly sand embankment collapse at a camp for displaced Palestinians in Deir Al-Balah, in the central Gaza Strip on November 9, 2026.

Save the Children said restrictions on deliveries of aid and reconstruction materials left people with few options to prepare for further storms.

“Four children who should have been safe and warm with their families instead lost their lives in an entirely preventable way,” said Ahmad Alhendawi, the organization’s regional director for the Middle East, referring to the children killed in the embankment collapse.

“Their deaths are a heartbreaking reminder that for children in Gaza, even bad weather can become deadly. Rain did not kill these children; they were killed by man-made conditions created by the Israeli authorities, forcing families to live in unsafe, inadequate shelters with nowhere else to go.

“Humanitarian organizations have repeatedly warned that without sufficient shelter materials and winter supplies, children would be put at risk. Those warnings are now being borne out in the most devastating way possible.”

“The international community cannot allow more children to die in disasters that are entirely foreseeable. No more families have to bury their children because of a storm.”

Gaza’s Civil Defense urged international organizations to provide safe shelters and move tents away from slopes, sandy areas and other locations at risk of collapse, the BBC reported.

But for families living under flimsy canvas, finding safer ground does not solve the problem of staying warm and dry.

Shireen Munir Ma’aruf, 24, a mother of two who is pregnant with her third child, was living in a tent in western Gaza City after being displaced from Beit Lahiya. She told the Israeli human rights group B’Tselem that she feared what lay ahead.

“Winter hasn’t even started yet and my tent and everything inside is flooded,” she said. “What will I do when the worst of it hits?”

World.title: Iraqi oil price for Asian markets reduced by $6 per barrel
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The price of Iraqi oil destined for Asian markets has seen a further reduction for December 2026 shipments, reflecting ongoing adjustments to official selling prices for crude in response to shifts in global oil markets.

Iraq’s State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) has decided to reduce the price of Basra Medium crude by $6 per barrel compared to the November pricing, setting the discount at $8.80 per barrel relative to the Oman/Dubai crude benchmark.

The reduction also extended to Basra Heavy crude; SOMO set its price for December at a discount of $11.80 per barrel against the Oman/Dubai average, compared to a discount of $5.80 per barrel in November.

The decisions follow months of dramatic swings in Iraqi oil discounts, interruptions to Gulf shipping, and an increase in the cost of insurance and transportation.

SOMO announced on Monday a reduction in the official selling price for Basra Medium crude destined for Asia for the month of December.

The state-owned firm set the price for this crude at a discount of $8.80 per barrel relative to the Oman/Dubai average, compared to a discount of $2.80 per barrel in the November pricing.

The company also set the official selling price for Basra Heavy crude destined for Asia in December at a discount of $11.80 per barrel.

This significant reduction in the price of Iraqi crude reflects an effort to enhance the attractiveness of Basra crude in Asian markets, which serve as the primary destination for the country’s oil exports.

World.title: Iraqi PM secretly visits Iran following Trump phone call
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – As part of regional mediation efforts, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi made an unexpected, secret visit to Tehran on Friday to meet with Iranian parliament speaker and senior negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf.

To help resolve the conflict between Iran and the United States, al-Zaidi’s short journey concentrated on diplomatic initiatives and de-escalation efforts.

The visit came after a phone conversation between al-Zaidi and US President Donald Trump, with the Iraqi government attempting to prevent the country from being involved in a larger regional conflict, according to reports quoting official and media sources.

Iranian officials, including top negotiator Ghalibaf, presented Tehran’s two-day plan at the discussions, stressing that Washington must respect Iran’s fundamental rights, lift sanctions, end naval blockade, and free frozen assets as part of the negotiations.

Iraqi Ambassador to Iran Yasser al-Hajjaj confirmed that a recent visit to Tehran—involving an Iraqi delegation or Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi—was private and unannounced, coinciding with reports of regional diplomatic discussions.

World.title: Iraqi, KRG PMs discuss 2027 federal budget
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi received on Monday the Prime Minister of the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG), Masrour Barzani, in Baghdad to discuss Iraqi Kurdistan’s financial entitlements and its share in the draft 2027 federal budget.

The precise amount allocated to the Kurdistan region of Iraq is a major source of disagreement. Approximately 12.7 percent is what the first draft budget suggests.

The KRG, on the other hand, is strongly advocating for 14.14 percent, claiming that the budget has to take into account Iraqi Kurdistan’s real population statistics from the most recent census.

Barzani has openly said that any distribution that falls short of this population-based proportion is unfair.

The discussions included establishing conclusive procedures to address persistent delays in the payment of salaries for Iraqi Kurdistan’s civil servants.

Recently, al-Zaidi reiterated Baghdad’s resolve to ensure that Kurdish public sector workers receive the same treatment as their colleagues in other Iraqi provinces.

The diplomatic effort tackles long-standing disagreements on constitutional rights, compliance with Iraqi Federal Court decisions, and oil income sharing.

The meeting takes place at a critical time. The Iraqi cabinet is scheduled to discuss and submit the finalized draft budget bill to parliament.

World.title: Iraq approaches OPEC to raise oil output ceiling
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair said that Iraq seeks to negotiate with OPEC to raise its oil output and obtain a larger export cap.

Although the country’s production capacity differs from its export capability, Khudair stated that Baghdad was still committed to the export quota set by OPEC.

Iraq’s discussions with OPEC took into account the challenges the country has faced over the past 50 years, as noted by Khudair.

The Iraqi minister indicated that Iraq deserves a rise in output to secure the financial revenues needed to expand infrastructure and implement government goals.

Additionally, Khudair reiterated Iraq’s commitment to the 4.43 million barrels per day production cap set by OPEC.

In early September, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi called for an increase in oil output to reach 10 million barrels per day by 2030.

According to al-Zaidi, Iraq’s oil output should be proportionate to its reserves, oil production capabilities, and the growing number of the population, allowing it to satisfy its residents’ needs as well as development requirements.

Iraq’s oil production reached approximately 4.5 million barrels per day by the end of 2025.

According to al-Zaidi, the Oil Ministry will invite major foreign oil firms to a conference to attract investments, expertise, and technologies.

World.title: Trump says Iran war ‘highly unlikely’ to resume
World.content:
Washington – US President Donald Trump cast doubt on renewed fighting with Iran, telling CNN it was “highly unlikely,” ahead of a meeting with mediator Qatar’s prime minister on Monday.

Trump has threatened to resume strikes in recent weeks, with US media reports suggesting that hostilities could restart after last Tuesday’s midterm elections.

The president told CNN in an interview on Sunday that renewed fighting was “highly unlikely,” but warned that his decision “depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement.”

“I would if necessary, but we hit them really hard. I hit them so hard. You don’t know how hard I hit them,” he said.

Trump is scheduled to meet Qatar’s Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, who is also the country’s foreign minister, at the White House on Monday.

The meeting will be Trump’s first with a foreign leader since a massive midterm loss that saw his Republican Party lose control of Congress.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi suggested on Sunday that peace talks had been paused while the political fallout of the vote was being assessed.

“For the past few days, there has been no more travel (by mediators), and the reason for this is the shock that the election results in the United States have caused to everyone,” Araghchi told state television.

“We now have to see how long it will take for them to digest these results, in order to determine how we are going to move forward,” he added.

– ‘They had enough’ –

Trump has acknowledged that the highly unpopular war with Iran — which began with US-Israeli strikes in late February — was at least partially responsible for the Republicans’ defeat.

Araghchi said Monday that the US president “clearly recognizes that the vast majority of Americans are disgusted with Israel.”

“Americans are evidently sick and tired of Israel bamboozling US administrations into Forever Wars,” Araghchi said on X. “They had enough. So has our region.”

In Sunday’s CNN interview, Trump once again suggested that the economic pressure Iran is under will force its leaders into accepting the United States’ terms.

“They’re a failing nation. It just came out, you saw this year, 301 percent inflation,” Trump claimed. “They’re withering away financially. We’ve hit them militarily. We could finish them off.”

Iran’s official figures put inflation at nearly 90 percent year-on-year in September.

Iranian state television said the island of Qeshm in the Strait of Hormuz was attacked overnight Sunday, hours after the official IRNA news agency reported two explosions there.

Various regional powers, including Qatar and Pakistan, have been trying for months without success to bring a definitive halt to the war.

Outright fighting has largely subsided, but Iran continues in its efforts to blockade the Strait of Hormuz, vital to global energy supplies, while the US Navy maintains its own counterblockade of Iranian ports.

World.title: Drone attack targets Khor Mor gas field in northern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A drone attack targeted on Sunday the Khor Mor gas field in northern Iraq, forcing joint field operator Dana Gas to halt production entirely.

The strike hit a liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) storage tank, causing a large fire that was later extinguished.

The facility is the main source of energy for the Kurdistan region of Iraq and the largest gas field there.

Between 2,500 and 2,800 megawatts of power output have been cut off due to the stoppage of gas operations, reducing 70 to 80 percent of the energy grid’s overall capacity.

Iraqi Kurdistan’s major cities, including Erbil, Sulaimaniyah, Duhok, Bazian, and Chamchamal, are no longer receiving direct electricity supply.

To safeguard vital infrastructure, including hospitals and water treatment facilities, Iraqi Kurdistan’s Ministry of Electricity declared that it is rerouting electricity from hydroelectric power plants and alternative fuel facilities.

Employees were evacuated to shelters, and no casualties or injuries have been reported, according to Dana Gas and Iraqi authorities.

The facility was temporarily closed in July due to security concerns resulting from escalating military tensions between the United States and Iran.

World.title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang, the scandal-hit AI visionary in a leather jacket
World.content:
New York – Chips made by US chip titan Nvidia push the boundaries of artificial intelligence, but its leader Jensen Huang is in the spotlight over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

Unknown to the public just four years ago, the 63-year-old is a powerful entrepreneur, drawing stadium crowds as he presents cutting-edge components essential to the development of AI tools like ChatGPT.

Media reports last week said US intelligence officials believe Huang grew close to a Chinese executive who was funneling information to Beijing.

Nvidia’s board said on Sunday it had opened a probe into the CEO and co-founder, who acknowledged having been unfaithful to his wife and said he was “deeply sorry.”

Big tech’s insatiable appetite for chips designed by Nvidia, known as Graphics Processing Units (GPUs), has catapulted the California chipmaker to a market valuation of $4.5 trillion, among the world’s largest.

Its meteoric rise has made Huang one of the world’s richest people — worth around $160 billion, according to Forbes — thanks to the roughly four percent stake he holds in the company he founded three decades ago with two friends in a Silicon Valley diner.

He has become a close informal adviser on AI to Donald Trump, traveling with the US president on Air Force One on a trip to Beijing earlier this year.

That is an area of concern to US officials who believe he has been involved with the alleged spy, Alice Huang, who is linked to a Singapore-based data center company, according to the New York Times.

Despite their shared surname, the pair are not related.

– Early life –

Born in Taipei in 1963, Jensen Huang — originally named Jen-Hsun — embodies the American success story.

At nine years old, he was sent away with his brother to boarding school in small-town Kentucky.

His uncle recommended the school to his Taiwanese parents believing it to be a prestigious institution, though it was actually a school for troubled youth.

Too young to be a student, Huang boarded there but attended a nearby public school alongside the children of tobacco farmers. With his poor English, he was bullied and forced to clean toilets — a two-year ordeal that transformed him.

“We worked really hard, we studied really hard, and the kids were really tough,” he recounted in an interview with US broadcaster NPR.

But “the ending of the story is I loved the time I was there,” Huang said.

Brought home by his parents who had by then settled in the northwestern US state of Oregon, he graduated from university at just 20 and joined AMD, then LSI Logic, to design chips — his passion.

But he wanted to go further and founded Nvidia in 1993 to “solve problems that normal computers can’t,” using semiconductors powerful enough to handle 3D graphics, he said during an interview on the “No Priors” podcast.

– ‘As fast as we can’ –

Nvidia created the first GPU in 1999, riding the intersection of video games, data centers, cloud computing and now generative AI.

Always dressed in a black T-shirt and leather jacket, Huang sports a Nvidia logo tattoo and has a taste for sports cars.

One former high-ranking Nvidia employee described him to AFP as “the most driven person” he’d ever met.

He has rejected calls to deliberately slow down AI development even as some insiders warn the technology could threaten human existence within a decade.

“That kind of narrative is dramatic, it gets a lot of attention,” but “it’s not grounded on facts,” he told CBS News in September.

“We should go as fast as we can” on AI, but labs should not release products that are not safe, he said.

– Street food –

On visits to his native Taiwan, Huang is treated like a megastar, with fans crowding him for autographs and selfies as journalists follow him to the barber shop and his favorite night market.

“He has created the phenomena because of his personal charm,” noted Wayne Lin of Witology Market Trend Research Institute.

“A person like him must be very busy and his schedule should be full every day meeting big bosses. But he remembers to eat street food when he comes to Taiwan,” he said, calling Huang “unusually friendly.”

Over the years, Nvidia has taken care to project a drama-free image of Huang.

But the former employee painted a more nuanced picture, describing a “very paradoxical” individual fiercely protective of his employees but also capable, within Nvidia’s executive circle, of “ripping people to shreds” over major mistakes or poor choices.

World.title: World Bank backs Iraq’s shift toward program and performance budgeting
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The World Bank reaffirmed its institutional support on Monday, November 9, 2026, for the Iraqi Ministry of Finance’s ongoing modernization agenda, focusing on technical requirements to transition Iraq’s fiscal planning toward a program- and performance-based budgeting framework.

According to a Ministry of Finance statement reported by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Senior Undersecretary Abdul-Hasan Jamal convened an extensive technical working session with a World Bank mission.

The deliberations were attended by the directors general of the Public Debt and Information Technology departments, alongside the ministry’s dedicated project implementation task force, to evaluate core prerequisites and execution roadmaps for the budgeting shift.

Jamal emphasized the necessity of finalizing statutory and regulatory frameworks, conducting rigorous cost-benefit assessments, and clearly designating spending units across line ministries.

He noted that moving away from conventional line-item budgeting to performance-driven fiscal management aligns directly with broader economic and administrative reform programs, ensuring cohesive institutional alignment among spending entities.

For its part, the World Bank delegation reiterated its commitment to supporting public financial management (PFM) reforms across Iraq, underlining that digitizing accounting frameworks and automating treasury workflows remain essential catalysts for curbing fiscal leakage, improving capital allocation, and enhancing aggregate expenditure efficiency.

World.title: 'Global capital for Sanatan pilgrimage': Akhilesh's big Ayodhya promise ahead of 2027 UP polls
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

chief

made a vow to transform

into the âglobal capital of Sanatan pilgrimageâ, pledging transparent temple administration, world-class infrastructure and measures to revive the local economy ahead of his proposed visit to the Ram Temple on December 12.

In a lengthy social media post, Yadav also accused the

BJP

of weakening the bond between Lord Ram and the Nishad community, promised to protect traditional boatmen and warned that those involved in alleged land and circle-rate scams in Ayodhya would face action if his party returned to power.

âWe are committed to restoring the honour and dignity of the city of Ayodhya,â Akhilesh said, alleging that the number of devotees and pilgrims visiting the temple town had been declining because of the hurt caused by the âtheft of the Ram templeâ.



He said the decline had directly affected the local economy and promised to reverse the trend.

âWe will both improve and transform it. By introducing transparent administration at Ayodhyaâs temple, we will also restore trust. By providing world-class infrastructure, we will make Ayodhya the âglobal capital of Sanatan pilgrimageâ,â he said.

The SP chief also promised measures to prevent the alleged mistreatment of poor people in the temple town, referring to an incident involving a woman and children collecting oil.





âWe will create an Ayodhya where no arrogant person can beat a poor woman or a boy or girl collecting oil and humiliate or oppress them,â he said.

The SP chief further said that if voted to power, his government would provide oil and ghee through the public distribution system. âOnce in government, we will also provide âoil and gheeâ in rations to meet the bodyâs nutritional needs,â he added.

He further invoked the association between Lord Ram and Nishadraj, a central figure in the Ramayana tradition, and accused the BJP of attempting to undermine the relationship.

âWe will promote traditional boating in Ayodhya, so that traditional boatmen benefit from it and the deep bond between Lord Ram and Nishadraj can be restored,â he said.

âThe BJP wants to break this bond because BJP supremacists never want anyone to remember any scene of Lord Ram and the PDA community embracing one another,â Yadav added.

PDA, or Pichhda, Dalit and Alpsankhyak (backward classes, Dalits and minorities), is the social coalition that the SP chief has been seeking to consolidate politically.

Akhilesh also targeted alleged irregularities in land transactions and the circle rates in Ayodhya, promising scrutiny of land records and action against those responsible. âWe will free Ayodhya from outside contractors and scrutinise land records. Outsiders are the ones who have looted Ayodhya,â he said.

âNo BJP leader or corrupt official involved in the massive circle-rate scam will escape. Their coffers, filled with the proceeds of Ayodhyaâs plunder, will be emptied,â he added.

The SP chief also called for legal action against people who insult religious deities and prominent figures, saying those who encourage such remarks should also be held accountable. âWe will also create a system to ensure that no foul-mouthed person can insult the deities or great figures of any religion, let alone those of Lord Ram or Lord Krishna, or go about freely after doing so,â he said.

Yadav further said that those encouraging people who make abusive remarks should also face consequences.

âThose who encourage such wicked people who utter abusive words are also complicit in their sin, and they too will be punished appropriately for their involvement in a conspiracy to disrupt social harmony,â he said.

CM Yogi Adityanath demands apology ahead of Akhilesh's Ayodhya visit

Akhilesh's post came amid a political exchange over his proposed December 12 visit to Ayodhya, where he is scheduled to visit the Ram Temple and Hanumangarhi along with his wife, Dimple Yadav. The visit, announced by former SP MLA Pawan Pandey, would be Akhilesh's first to the Ram Temple since its inauguration in January 2024.

Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Saturday took an apparent swipe at the SP chief, saying those who had ordered firing on Ram devotees and subjected saints to lathicharge should apologise before visiting the temple.

âThose who had neglected and insulted (Ayodhya), who had opened fire on Ram devotees and subjected saints to lathicharge, should certainly come to Ayodhya, but only after apologising.

Let them apologise once to Ram devotees and once to the saints. Let them repent for their actions,â Adityanath said at the 10th edition of Deepotsav in Ayodhya, according to PTI.

Although he did not name any person or the party, the remarks came hours after the announcement of the proposed temple visit.

âThere was a time when even uttering the name of Shri Ram in Ayodhya invited lathis and bullets. Banning the very name of Ram in this city was a sin. Ayodhya was neglected and almost consigned to oblivion. Today, that very Ayodhya has come alive again, reminding us of the Treta Yuga,â he said.

World.title: Ahead of peace talks, Zelenskyy seeks PM Modi's help on ceasefire
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Ahead of the Abu Dhabi peace talks, PM Narendra Modi and Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy spoke Monday with the latter briefing the PM about latest developments related to the Russia-Ukraine conflict and Modi conveying Indiaâs "firm commitment" to contributing in every possible way towards a peaceful resolution of the Russia-Ukraine war.

The conversation took place a day before the trilateral peace dialogue involving Russia, Ukraine and the US in Abu Dhabi, and amid renewed Russian strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure. Ahead of the talks, where India's recent peace proposals are likely to be discussed too, India remained engaged with both sides on diplomatic initiatives as foreign minister S Jaishankar too spoke to his Russian counterpart Sergey Lavrov.



Zelenskyy recalled Modi's latest peace message to President Vladimir Putin that it was time now to end the "endless war" and urged India to take more steps towards a ceasefire that can ensure food and energy security. Modi said in a post on X that he and Zelenskyy had a productive conversation â their first since they met on the margins of the G7 summit in France in June.

Modi's message to Zelenskyy expressing India's readiness to facilitate peace is not new, but its timing is significant as this was the first time they spoke after Jaishankar revealed in early October India was actively mediating for establishment of safe corridors in the Black Sea for grain and energy exports.





"We reviewed our wide-ranging bilateral cooperation and agreed to further strengthen India-Ukraine ties. I thanked President Zelenskyy for sharing his perspectives on the ongoing conflict, its humanitarian aspects and various efforts to restore peace," said Modi in his own readout of the talks.

Ukraine believes Russia has not responded positively to India's Black Sea shipping proposal and the call to end targeting of its energy sector.

"The Prime Minister has said more than once, including directly to the Russian âleader, â that now is the time to end the war, not to continue it," said Zelenskyy on X after his talks with Modi, urging India to identify steps it can take and also talks it can pursue with other leaders to bring the conflict to an end.

âFood security could be one such area. We discussed Russia's blocking of grain exports via the Black Sea. India is ready to mediate in establishing food corridors, and we are counting on these efforts to continue,â said the Ukrainian president.

Zelenskyy also said Ukraine had always taken a constructive approach, and Russia must show the same readiness to de-escalate.

âRussia must understand that the global economy and hundreds of millions of people around the world are suffering because of blocked sea routes. We agreed that our teams will stay in touch on these and other bilateral issues,â he said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

An Indian readout said Modi reaffirmed Indiaâs human-centric approach and reiterated Indiaâs consistent position that the conflict must be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy.

The 4th round of Russia-Ukraine peace talks mediated by the US are scheduled to begin in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday. While the core negotiations are structured as trilateral sessions involving Russia, Ukraine, and the US, Ukrainian delegation will hold separate coordination meetings with their European and Nato allies including France, Germany and the UK on the sidelines.

World.title: Fearing winter polls, Ladakh political parties, social bodies plan protests
World.content:
SRINAGAR: Political parties and civil society groups in Ladakh, apprehensive that the administration might hold Hill Council elections in Dec, on Monday said a winter election schedule would disenfranchise a significant section of the population as nearly 25% of Ladakhis migrate to other parts of the country during the harsh winter season.

In Kargil, political parties and religious and social organisations called for a complete shutdown on Tuesday and a candlelight march in the evening, demanding deferment of the elections. In Leh, the Leh Apex Body (LAB) threatened to launch an agitation within the next few days. The administration, however, has not announced any dates for hill council polls as yet. Senior Ladakh administration officials were not available for comment.



âFor the past month we have been witnessing a series of notifications and orders and a flawed delimitation exercise. No one has been consulted or taken into confidence. The UT administration is once again imposing decisions on people,â Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) co-chairman Sajjad Kargili said at a news conference in Kargil. Flanked by Ladakh MP Mohmad Haneefa and other political and religious leaders, Kargili said 20% to 25% of Ladakhâs population, particularly elderly people, students and members of the business community, migrates outside the region during winter.





Despite this, he said, the administration appears adamant about holding Hill Council elections in Dec. âThis is an inappropriate and unwise decision.â Kargili said the people of Kargil have decided to observe a complete shutdown Tuesday.

Haneefa said the proposed elections should not come at the cost of peopleâs democratic rights, pointing to harsh weather, difficult terrain, road closures and disrupted connectivity.

Haneefa said he had urged the L-G to reconsider and defer the election schedule, allowing sufficient time for a comprehensive revision of electoral rolls and consultations with all stakeholders.

In Leh, Leh Apex Body co-chairman Chering Dorjay Lakrook also urged the administration to postpone the elections until April or May next year, saying constituencies should first be properly delineated to ensure wider public participation.

Addressing a news conference alongside members of All Goba Association and Ladakh Buddhist Association members, Lakrook said holding elections after winter would allow more people to participate. Lakrook also announced that the Leh Apex Body would launch an agitation within two to three days, saying the movement would demonstrate its public support. âWe were supposed to be invited to the talks with the ministry of home affairs in Delhi on Oct 22, but we were not.

The administration is taking us for granted. It is time for Ladakhis to wake up and stand up for their rights,â he said.

World.title: Chinese nationals stream from poor localities of Dhaka, claim those are in Delhi: Report
World.content:
The setting is Dhaka, but the audience in China is told it is Delhi. An estimated total of over 150 Chinese nationals have been livestreaming from an underprivileged neighbourhood in Dhaka, falsely presenting it to their viewers back home as everyday life in India, an investigation by the Bangladeshi newspaper Prothom Alo revealed.

Equipped with two smartphones each - one used to stream live and the other with scripts - they broadcast from early morning until late at night. According to the report, the streamers focus on Sector 12 and Tekpara, which are dense, low-income settlements along a canal in Uttara town, located north of Dhaka, where they film along the tin-roofed houses. Local guides, hired for Tk 700 to Tk 800 (Rs 525-Rs 600) a day, assist the Chinese nationals in navigating the area.



While most of these creators refused to speak to Prothom Alo, some only gave their names and nationality. A Chinese national named Fangyou, after being persuaded by a guide, said that such streams are broadcast on China-based platforms such as WeChat and Douyin (the mainland version of TikTok) as "part of product promotion activities".

Google translations of their commentary, verified by four Bangladeshis who know Chinese, revealed misrepresentation.





In one instance, a Chinese woman identifying herself as Mianmian showed the tin huts and said, "This is Delhi. Their homes are extremely dirty... and the law-and-order situation is poor."

At a bridge flanked by tea stalls, another creator named Wang Wei could be heard telling his audience that locals were drinking "cow urine tea" prepared with contaminated river water. Some streamers claimed they were Chinese women married to Indian men living in these neighbourhoods, while promoting Chinese air conditioner brands seen on building walls.

Locals, who talked to Prothom Alo, said that streamers routinely enter homes unannounced, sometimes even filming into bathrooms. World.title: SC: Govt has wide powers to compulsorily retire staffer, improve efficiency
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Supreme Court has ruled govt has wide powers to compulsorily retire an employee to improve efficiency of administration and that the person aggrieved cannot challenge such a decision on the ground that other similarly placed employees have not met the same fate.

Upholding Chhattisgarh govt's decision to compulsorily retire five employees, a bench of Justices Manmohan and Shree Chandrashekhar said the principle of "every person must be heard before being punished", as enshrined in Article 311(2) of Constitution, is not applicable to cases of compulsory retirement because it is neither punitive nor casts aspersion upon an employee's conduct.

Justice Manmohan said, "The decision is founded upon the subjective satisfaction of competent authority that the employee's continued retention in service is no longer conducive to public interest."



Retirement must be based on bona fide assessment, says SC

Writing the judgement, Justice Manmohan said, âThe ultimate assessment as to whether an officer has become âdead woodâ or whether his continuance would be detrimental to administrative efficiency falls within the domain of the executive.â

Chhattisgarh additional advocate general Rajat Nair said decisions to compulsorily retire the five âassistantâ grade officers was arrived at in public interest for maintaining efficiency of administration after a two-tier scrutiny of their performance, efficiency, track records, integrity and annual confidential records.





When such decisions are challenged by aggrieved employees, courts need to re-appreciate or re-evaluate material considered by authorities. âThe court is concerned only with whether relevant material existed, whether such material was taken into consideration by competent authority, and whether the conclusion drawn therefrom is one which a reasonable person could have arrived at,â it said while rejecting the appeals.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

It said, âThe power to compulsorily retire a govt servant under applicable service rules is of wide amplitude and is conditional principally by the requirement that the authority must form its opinion bona fide and upon relevant material. Mere fact that another officer, who may appear similarly placed, was not compulsorily retired cannot constitute a valid defence to an otherwise lawful order of compulsory retirement.

World.title: Now, Cong-led Keralam govt follows Karnataka on 'ethanol test'
World.content:
BENGALURU/NEW DELHI/T'PURAM: Following in Congress-governed Karnataka's footsteps, the Congress-led govt of Keralam Monday started collecting petrol samples to test whether their ethanol content was more than the prescribed 20%, setting up a likely Centre-state confrontation over E20 fuel.

Keralam civil supplies minister Anoop Jacob said officials collected six samples each from nine petrol pumps across Thiruvananthapuram, Ernakulam, Kozhikode and Kannur, in the presence of OMC representatives.

PESO-approved bottles and trained officials were used, he said, adding that further rounds of testing would follow and prosecution would be initiated if excess blending was detected.

This prompted Union minister of state for petroleum Suresh Gopi to say that states were free to conduct tests but they should avoid political mudslinging.



"Let them conduct the tests, whether it is Karnataka or Keralam govt. We have scientific support for it," he said. The minister warned that those creating controversies for political purposes would have to face consequences. Gopi said Centre had permitted 20% blending after assessing scientific feasibility and was implementing the transition gradually.

On Monday, Karnataka defended its third-party laboratory findings about ethanol levels of up to 31.2%, rejecting a joint rebuttal by three oil marketing companies - IOCL, BPCL and HPCL.





State food and civil supplies minister Rizwan Arshad termed objections raised by the three OMCs "illogical" and accused them of trying to push for a fresh joint survey after recalibrating the ethanol mix.

He said state govt would send its findings to Centre, seek changes in testing protocols and demand discounted prices for E20 petrol, stressing that higher ethanol content reduced mileage and raised the effective cost for consumers.

Arshad said alleged blending of up to 30% was happening at six terminals where ethanol was mixed with petrol before distribution, not at retail outlets. Karnataka said authorised officials followed prescribed sampling procedures, with labels jointly signed by officials and dealers. After OMC laboratories failed to provide ethanol percentages for the initial 63 samples, the state sent them to NABL-accredited, ISO-certified third-party laboratories.

World.title: Adult vaccination remains low; elderly miss cover against flu and shingles
World.content:
Adult vaccination remains low; elderly miss cover against flu and shingles

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Despite vaccines being available to prevent several infections that can be particularly serious for older people, adult immunisation remains low in India. Influenza, pneumococcal disease and shingles are among the key vaccine-preventable illnesses that pose a risk to older people, but studies point to poor awareness and low uptake of these vaccines. Ahead of World Immunisation Day Tuesday (Nov 10), the findings highlight a significant gap in protection beyond childhood.A multicentre study of 4,998 people aged 60 and above across Chennai, Ballabgarh, Kolkata and Pune found only 1.4% had ever received an influenza vaccine. While just 19.7% had heard of influenza, 35.9% considered vaccines safe and 65.3% were unwilling to pay for vaccination. However, uptake rose to 29.7% when vaccines were offered free of cost at community health camps.Published in 'BMC Public Health' in 2026, the study highlights gaps in awareness, acceptance and access to vaccination among older people.The disease burden is substantial. A separate study published in 'Influenza and Other Respiratory Viruses' in April 2026 estimated that influenza among Indians aged 60 and above accounted for 5.3 million respiratory infections, 36,149 hospitalisations and 84,613 deaths in 2021.The researchers found that an annual influenza vaccination programme for older adults could be cost-effective under most of the scenarios assessed."Influenza and pneumococcal infections cause a significant burden among older Indians, accounting for an estimated 1.2 lakh deaths annually. Studies show that influenza vaccination can reduce influenza-associated pneumonia cases by 52% and deaths by 70%, while pneumococcal vaccination can lower hospitalisations by around 27% and deaths by 34%. Yet vaccination coverage among the elderly remains very low," said Dr Neetu Jain, senior consultant, pulmonology, critical care and sleep medicine, PSRI Hospital."Annual flu and pneumococcal vaccination is particularly important for people above 60 and those with COPD, asthma, diabetes or heart disease, as infections can lead to serious complications, including respiratory failure and prolonged hospitalisation," she said.Evidence is also emerging of the economic value of pneumococcal vaccination. A study published in 'Infectious Diseases and Therapy' in Oct 2026 examined the cost-effectiveness of a single dose of the 20-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV20) for older adults and people at higher risk. It found that the vaccine could be a cost-effective option compared with existing vaccination approaches.Another infection of concern among older adults is shingles, caused by reactivation of the virus responsible for chicken pox. It can lead to prolonged nerve pain, known as post-herpetic neuralgia. A 2026 paper in 'Indian Journal of Community Medicine' noted the lack of robust population-based data on shingles in India, while citing an estimate of around 45 lakh cases annually. An Indian phase-3 trial of the recombinant zoster vaccine, published in 'Vaccine' in 2025, reported an immune response in 85.7% of participants aged 50 and above."Influenza and pneumococcal vaccines can reduce cases of severe illness, hospitalisation and complications, particularly among older people and those with chronic conditions such as diabetes, heart disease and COPD. Both are non-live vaccines and can be given to elderly people, including those with multiple conditions," said Dr Jatin Ahuja, infectious disease specialist, Apollo Hospitals, Delhi."India also needs to expand adult vaccination to cover shingles. The two-dose recombinant zoster vaccine is recommended for adults aged 50 and above and offers over 90% protection. Tdap or Td boosters, hepatitis B and, where indicated, Covid-19 and RSV vaccines should also be considered," he said.Goa has taken a step towards expanding vaccination beyond childhood through its Life-course Immunisation Policy 2026-2036, launched in Sept. The policy identifies influenza, pneumococcal and hepatitis B vaccination among its priorities for elderly, those with chronic illnesses, immunocompromised individuals and healthcare workers.

World.title: How AI is reshaping China’s universities
World.content:
In September 2026, China’s government unveiled an ambitious 10-year plan to reform its universities. Driving the change is an increasingly challenging job market for the country’s close to 13 million college graduates, who are facing the twin disruptions of AI and a slowing economy. Under the plan, dozens of graduate programmes are being disbanded, while universities themselves will be categorised and tasked with either pursuing research, applications or skills development.

A combination of factors, some not too dissimilar to the current challenges in India’s own job market, has left policymakers grappling with a tepid job market and a vast number of graduates facing dim job prospects. Top of the list is a mismatch in skills between graduates and what companies are seeking. Depressed economic sentiment has also led companies to cut back on hiring, with the prolonged structural slowdown in the real estate market dragging down growth. AI is the third disruptive force, changing rapidly how the marketplace views and values skills.

World.title: France blames Iran for cyberattack on supermarket fridges
World.content:
France on Monday blamed Iran for last month's massive cyberattack on supermarket fridges, summoned the Iranian ambassador and said it would seek European sanctions against those responsible for the attack.

The October 12 attack sent refrigerator temperatures soaring, affecting about 700 of the country's 10,000 supermarkets. In a statement Monday, prosecutors in Paris said they found that Iran's paramilitary Revolutionary Guard was behind the large-scale cyberattack.

The French Foreign Ministry condemned the attack “in the strongest possible terms,” and French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot, speaking on the sidelines of G7 talks in Paris, said the Iranian ambassador was being summoned to “strongly protest against this extremely serious act.”

“This is an attack of unprecedented scale and aggressiveness,” Mr. Barrot said. “It is the first large-scale cyberattack aimed at sabotage on French soil, and it represents a major threat to our national interests and the security of the French people. That is why it will not go unanswered.”

“We will impose sanctions at the European level against all those responsible for this attack,” he added, vowing to take “any other measures needed” to respond to it and deter future attacks.

Paris prosecutor Laure Beccuau said in a statement that a formal judicial investigation was opened Monday into suspected organised cybercrime with the aggravating circumstance of “having been committed to serve the interests of a foreign power — in this case, Iran."

The investigation targets Shahid Kaveh, the leader of an Iranian group described as a “cyber unit” affiliated with Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, as well as his two deputies and any other individuals who might be identified in connection with the case.

Investigators found that the attackers had used Farsi and IP addresses linked to devices located in Iran, Mr. Beccuau said. The Paris prosecutor's office is seeking international arrest warrants, she said.

In the early hours of October 12, attackers remotely took control of refrigeration systems in hundreds of supermarkets and independent stores across France. Temperatures reached 50 degrees Celsius for about six hours, forcing stores to discard fresh and frozen goods. The Intermarche supermarket chain reported losses of “tens of millions of euros” in a single day.

World.title: Nvidia, CEO Huang sued over disclosures related to suspected Chinese spy
World.content:
Nvidia ​and Chief Executive Jensen Huang were sued on ‌Monday (November 9, 2026) in a proposed class action accusing ​them of defrauding shareholders by ⁠concealing Huang's ties with a suspected Chinese spy.

According to a complaint filed in federal court ‌in San Jose, California, the defendants misled shareholders about Huang's alleged affair with ‌Alice Huang, a former executive ‌of Singapore-based ⁠Megaspeed who is not related to ⁠him, and did not disclose that the matter raised national security concerns that threatened Nvidia's reputation and ​business prospects.

The New ‌York Times reported last month about the alleged relationship, and that U.S. authorities had concluded Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence ‌asset.

Nvidia did not immediately respond to ​a request for comment.

Jensen Huang told Nvidia's employees he had ⁠been unfaithful to his wife, without disclosing details of the alleged relationship.

He co-founded Nvidia and ‌has led the Santa Clara, California-based company as it became the world's most valuable chipmaker and made him one of the world's most prominent symbols of the artificial intelligence boom.

Nvidia announced a probe into ‌the matter on Sunday (November 8, 2026). Its shares closed down ​4.3% on Monday (November 9, 2026), reducing Nvidia's market capitalisation by approximately $190 billion. The lawsuit ⁠was filed five minutes after the U.S. stock ⁠market closed.

It is common for shareholders to sue companies after unexpected share ‌price declines. Nvidia shareholders, led by Mark Kistenmacher are seeking unspecified damages from ​the defendants.

World.title: Mystery of a missing sewage treatment plant tells the tale of the lake in Krishnakanth Park
World.content:
The lake inside the Krishnakath Park in Yousufguda has come a full circle over the past two decades, before the recent announcement by the Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Development Agency (HYDRAA) revealing plans to develop and restore the lake.

HYDRAA Commissioner A.V. Ranganath is taking special interest in expansion of the lake by four times its existing size, in order to impound the storm water that inundates Ameerpet and surrounding localities downstream every time it rains.

Currently restricted to about three acres and divided into three separate ponds with interconnecting canals, the water body is now set to be increased to 12 acres.

Work to fell and translocate trees from the park is already underway, with 34 trees marked for felling and 156 for translocation.

This initiative will largely reduce the 22-acre park space and drown its lawns, trees, gazebos and other facilities originally established 22 years ago. The project pivots on the argument that the entire park stands on what was originally a lake.

The lake, in fact, is a textbook example of how governments squander public money with no attention to sustainability or accountability. A simple search for a sewage treatment plant which has disappeared over the years lays bare the whole story.

The Sewage Treatment Plant (STP) was first established way back in 2003-04, with the intention of filling the three ponds constructed as part of the park’s development. The park was launched in 2004, by the then chief minister of the joint state of Andhra Pradesh, N. Chandrababu Naidu.

“There was no lake. Before the park, it was a colossal garbage dump. We got down to the daunting task of clearing all the trash in order to build a beautiful park there. Digging very deep, we built strong gazebos with granite, despite objections that the foundations would be at risk due to enormous amounts of rubble underneath. The three ponds were built so as to provide water for the greenery,” shared N. Chandramohan Reddy, who was then the Director, Urban Forestry, of Hyderabad Municipal Corporation.

Ramaraju, a senior citizen from Kalyan Nagar remembers a huge 22-acre lake at the location which had actually provided water for the crops.

“There was this heavy cascade of water that flowed from the lake through Madhura Nagar, and I remember seeing paddy fields on both sides during 1980s. Eventually with city development, sewage and industrial waste started flowing into the lake, and later it was turned into garbage dump,” Mr. Ramaraju reminisced.

G. Satyanarayana, another resident who served as the President of the Federation of Colony Welfare Associations, recalled the story that the garbage heap, when removed, revealed several animal carcasses dumped there over the years.

“I was told that the workers collapsed unable to bear the stench. Even after the park was laid, we fought against the garbage dump,” Mr. Satyanarayana said. The dump later became garbage collection centre of the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation.

As per the details shared by the engineering officials who worked on the park, an STP was built on the South-West corner of the park with 0.6 million litre treatment capacity per day (MLD), complete with facilities for filtration, aeration and sedimentation. A pipeline was laid from the STP to the lake for treated water. Another pipeline brought fresh storm water from the North-Eastern side, and a 12-feet stormwater drain running through the park emptied into the lake when overflowing.

Rank sewage flows through the drain now, though it does not enter the lake. In fact, over the two decades, the lake filled up only seasonally. It stayed dry in summer, as it should, and filled up post monsoon, indicating that the sewage was successfully thwarted from entering it.

HYDRAA chief A.V.Ranganath, sharing the ₹7.5 crore development plan for the lake, informed that a brand new STP with a capacity to treat 1-2 MLD sewage would be built inside the park, in order to bring purified water to the expanded lake. He has no inkling about the previous STP, nor about the stormwater drainage links to the lake.

The STP which slipped into oblivion now, remained defunct for most part of its existence owing to lack of maintenance. It was still under reckoning till 2021, as vouched by a Central Pollution Control Board report which mentioned it as ‘non-operational’. There was no information from GHMC about de-commissioning the STP.

The location of the STP now falls into the garbage transfer station managed Hyderabad Integrated Municipal Solid Waste Limited (HIMSW) which is a special purpose vehicle launched by Renvion-- a freshly rebranded version of the Ramky Enviro Engineers Limited. Entry into the facility is strictly manned.

An analysis of the Google Earth satellite images reveals that the STP was filled up starting from May, 2021, and structures of the transfer station were raised on it. Compound wall separating the transfer station from the STP was pulled down. Incidentally, 2021 was also the year when the transfer station was handed over to the HIMSW.

When queried about the STP, Renvion replied through their Public Relations agency, that the waste collection centre was handed over to HIMSW in 2021, which developed a modern transfer station within the premises given by GHMC. All the necessary approvals for the improvements were vetted and approved by GHMC and EPTRI. Renvion categorically denied the existence of any STP in the transfer station. A query to the GHMC Commissioner R.V. Karnan remained unanswered.

World.title: CSIR-CCMB team identifies potential new targets to fight Tuberculosis
World.content:
A team of scientists at the CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CCMB) has identified critical weaknesses in the bacterium that causes Tuberculosis (TB), a finding that could pave the way for the development of new treatments against one of the world’s deadliest infectious diseases.

The discovery is particularly significant for India, which accounts for nearly a quarter of global TB cases and about a third of drug-resistant infections, according to the World Health Organisation’s Global TB Report 2025. Drug-resistant TB remains a major public health challenge, as treatment requires a combination of antibiotics taken over several months and is becoming increasingly difficult due to the emergence of resistant strains.

Led by CCMB Director Vinay Kumar Nandicoori, the research team mapped the protein export machinery of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), the bacterium responsible for TB. The study sheds light on how the pathogen transports proteins within and outside its cells, a process essential for its growth, survival and ability to cause disease.

The research was carried out by joint first authors Priyadarshini Sanyal and Jagadeeshwari Uppada in collaboration with scientists from the Institute of Mathematical Sciences, Chennai, led by Areejit Samal, and the Translational Health Science and Technology Institute, Faridabad.

Using a combination of computational modelling and laboratory experiments, the researchers identified 92 key components and nearly 200 molecular reactions involved in the bacterium’s protein transport network. These included the general Sec pathway, the Twin-Arginine Translocation (Tat) system and the specialised ESX secretion systems unique to this group of bacteria.

“Protein secretion acts like a delivery system inside the bacterium and is vital for its survival,” said Dr Uppada. The team focused on two major secretion pathways, SecA1 and Tat, employing CRISPR-based gene-silencing technology to reduce their activity. The results were striking: bacterial growth declined sharply both in laboratory cultures and inside immune cells, demonstrating that both pathways are essential for the pathogen’s survival.

Dr Priyadarshini Sanyal said further analysis revealed that disrupting these systems affected the export of more than 100 proteins in the SecA1 pathway and around 140 proteins linked to the Tat system. Researchers also observed structural damage to the bacterial cell membrane, making it unstable and more permeable. Proteins that normally remain inside the bacterium began leaking into the surrounding environment.

Dr Nandicoori said that these changes highlight the close connection between protein secretion and the maintenance of the bacterial cell envelope, a key factor behind TB’s persistence and resistance to treatment. The findings, published in the peer-reviewed journal Molecular & Cellular Proteomics, could help researchers identify new drug targets, although translating the discovery into effective medicines will require several more years of research.

World.title: Trump says FBI looking into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with 'Chinese agent'
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump said Monday (November 9, 2026) that the FBI is investigating Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese government agent, but said he doesn't think the executive who has helped to develop artificial intelligence has a reason to worry.
